coll.how.folioFree.source: On page {page} of {folio}, for {aurum, number} Aurum. Open the Folios in the shop, the gem on the pause screen.

coll.how.folioGilded.source: On page {page} of {folio}, for {aurum, number} Aurum, once that folio is unlocked. Open the Folios in the shop, the gem on the pause screen.

coll.how.giftThanks.source: A gift to every player who had an account when the Storefront update came out.

coll.how.guildShop.source: Buy it on the Shop page of the Guild window for {price} of your own silver. It shows your guild's arms.

coll.how.hunt.source: Clear {n} bounties from the towns’ bounty boards. Every character of your account counts.

coll.how.mastery.source: Reach Master in {profession} on a living character of your account.

coll.how.sea.source: Help slay {n} Sea Serpents. One serpent a day counts.

coll.how.shopAurum.source: Buy it from the shop, the gem on the pause screen, for {aurum, number} Aurum.

coll.how.shopDeal.source: Buy it from the shop, the gem on the pause screen, for {aurum, number} Aurum. On a day it is a deal, it costs {deal, number} Aurum.

coll.how.shopPieceAurum.source: Buy it from the shop, the gem on the pause screen, for {aurum, number} Aurum. The Eternal Set gives it with the other four for {set, number} Aurum.

coll.how.wyrmrider.source: Tame a brass Dwarven Dragon. Each player who dealt it real damage has a chance of one in {n} when it falls.

coll.look.aetherium.source: A coil of aetherium-blue light wound with brass, turning about you from your feet to over your head.

coll.look.aetherwings.source: Wings of flowing pale-blue light from your back, the developers' Seraph Wings in aetherium's glow.

coll.look.dominion.source: A ring of Daedric script burning crimson on black at your feet, black thorns out from it and embers rising.

coll.look.eternal.source: A cape of blue-violet fire on your back, flowing as you move, wisps of flame trailing behind you.

coll.look.gildedcoil.source: The Aetherium Coil gilded and brighter, gold motes rising through it.

coll.look.vampirichaze.source: A dark violet haze smouldering about you, drops of blood rising from the ground like embers and turning into Daedric runes.

coll.looks.how.source: Every armour piece, shield and weapon you hold adds its look here. A Clothing Store, an Armorer or a Weaponsmith can give a piece you wear any look of its kind, for gold.

coll.looks.howBuy.source: To collect {name}: buy it at a shop.

coll.looks.howGet.source: To collect {name}: buy it, find it or make it.

coll.looks.wearAt.source: Over any piece of its kind ({kind}), at a Clothing Store, an Armorer or a Weaponsmith, for {gold, number} gold.

coll.trophies.how.source: A named beast from a bounty board gives one, and so does a Trophy Hunter's clean pelt of a grade 5 or 6 body.

coll.tunes.how.source: Foes sometimes drop sheet music. Use a sheet to add its tune. Make a placed piece a Music box in your house to play them.

credits.ambientText.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with the author’s own lines.

credits.ambientText.what.source: Now and then, a short line about your surroundings: 918 written by the author, chosen by the kind of place or dungeon you are in, the hour and the weather. It stays quiet indoors and waits longer after each line.

credits.basicRoads.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. The road painter is under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut).

credits.basicRoads.what.source: Roads and tracks across the Iliac Bay, from the author’s hand-drawn network, painted into the ground. Shown in both skins and on the map.

credits.betterAmbience.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License, with the 29 sound clips the mod uses, from the author’s repository. Its rain and snow particle changes are not included.

credits.betterAmbience.what.source: The camera shakes when you are hurt, more for bigger hits. Each dungeon gets its own fog color and light, and an echo on every sound. Rain can be heard, muffled, indoors and at dungeon entrances. Its own footsteps with an armor clank stay off while Immersive Footsteps is on, as that mod’s author asks.

credits.classSkins.terms.source: Used with the artists’ permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license. Its 1,683 pictures are included unchanged.

credits.classSkins.what.source: Daggerfall’s classes as looks for your character in third person: acrobat, assassin, burglar, bounty hunter, dark acolyte, Dark Brotherhood, healer, monk, nightblade, pirate and sorcerer, most in both sexes, plus the original adventurer, in 20 redrawn sprite sheets. Pick one on your profile’s Skin card.

credits.climatesCalories.terms.source: Reworked from the mod’s rules with the author’s permission, passed on by Mac. Its numbers were the starting point, and its own art is used for spoiled food, raw meat and the waterskin.

credits.climatesCalories.what.source: Survival. You feel the temperature from the climate, season, hour, weather, clothes and armor. Hunger, thirst, sleep and wetness are needs, food spoils, you can make camp and light campfires, and where you sleep matters. There are four tiers in Settings: Off, Boons (the default: neglect costs nothing, and staying fed, watered and rested gives bonuses), Casual (neglect only borrows stamina, which comes back once the need is met) and Hard (needs can hurt your attributes and health and make you sick).

credits.comeSailAway.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with his own pictures and sounds. Some wave textures are rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

credits.comeSailAway.what.source: A boat of your own to sail. Buy one as parts or as a deed, put it in the water (near a port for a deed) and take the helm. Row with the oars, or raise the sails, trim them to the wind and let it carry you. Pack the boat up to carry it with you. Includes his boats, sails, oars, wind gauge, waves and sounds.

credits.contact.forumsOrNexus.source: {author}, through the DFU forums ({forums}) or the Nexus page ({page})

credits.daggerfall.what.source: The original game. All of its art, sound, text and world data are read from your own copy’s ARENA2 folder. None of it is included here.

credits.dex.terms.source: Ported from the shipped bundle and the authors’ own source; their art carried byte for byte (Daggerfall’s own sprites among it rebuilt from your files) - see vendor/daggerfall-enemy-expansion/README.md for the permission record.

credits.dex.what.source: Fifty new enemies and the encounter tables they come from (DEX): goblins, trolls that get back up, minotaurs, golems, Dwarven centurions, mounted knights, necromancers, witches, the Vengeful King Lysandus and more, ported from the authors’ own source, in Kamer’s and Kab’s art - Daggerfall’s own sprites among it, some under their paint - and in Morrowind’s bodies where Morrowind has the creature.

credits.dfo.what.source: The engine and systems this project was forked from. Maintained for Daggerfall Forever by Alex 13 Uslavtsev.

credits.dfu.what.source: This game began as a rewrite of Daggerfall Unity and still uses it as its reference. Its quest scripts, book index, settings tables, game text table, interaction-mode icons and mouse cursor are included unchanged (MIT License).

credits.diverseWeapons.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. The script is under the MIT License, and the sprites are the author’s own paintings.

credits.diverseWeapons.what.source: First-person sprites for 18 weapons in every metal, plain and enchanted, where the original game has one sprite per weapon class. Includes double-size idle sprites for Weapon Widget and matching inventory icons.

credits.dynamicSkies.what.source: The sky with Enhanced environments on: a sun and atmosphere (built on Feral Pug’s extension of Unity’s procedural sky), 2 cloud layers for each weather, twinkling stars, Masser and Secunda moving through their phases, its own fog colors and distances, longer sunrises and sunsets, lightning flashes in storms, and pixel snow. The shader, presets and textures are the mod’s own. The Classic skin keeps Daggerfall’s painted sky.

credits.eyeOfTheBeholder.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 3,035 sprites.

credits.eyeOfTheBeholder.what.source: Third person without Morrowind data. Scroll the mouse wheel to swing the camera out behind your shoulder. It moves clear of walls, and you are drawn as the mod’s own sprite from 8 directions, standing, walking, attacking and casting, on foot or riding.

credits.foraging.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with his own quests and textures, and 6 bugs fixed.

credits.foraging.what.source: Make a living in the wilderness. Use a Wood-Axe to chop wood, a Pick-Axe to mine gems and metals, a Sickle to cut plants, a Spade to rob graves, a Fishing-Net to fish and a Basket to forage for food. It works by daylight, away from towns and enemies, depending on your attributes, the climate and the season. You can also fetch firewood for commoners and nobles. Its quests use 4 actions from Jagget’s Quest Actions Extension, rewritten here with thanks.

credits.grimoireUi.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. The pictures and fonts are the author’s own art, included unchanged.

credits.grimoireUi.what.source: Daggerfall’s screens redrawn at three times the detail, with parchment and wood instead of stone, a spellbook that looks like a book, and new lettering in two fonts. Choose it under Overhauls, on the UI Overhaul card.

credits.handheldTorches.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own textures.

credits.handheldTorches.what.source: Carrying a light takes a free hand. Drawing a two-handed weapon stows or drops your torch, and it lights again when your hand is free. Keys light, put out, drop and throw a torch, and a thrown torch can set an enemy alight. In first person you see your hand holding the light. Dropped torches keep burning, light the room, can be picked up and stay after a save.

credits.horseCart.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own horse art.

credits.horseCart.what.source: Your horse and wagon stay in the world. They wait where you dismount, or follow you or stay on command. Hitch the horse to the wagon, mount by walking up to them, and call them to you outdoors. Reach the wagon from an entrance it is parked near. Its load shows by weight and its wheels turn. Online, other players see them where you left them.

credits.iliacPuddle.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. The coastline is rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

credits.iliacPuddle.what.source: Makes the Iliac Bay a real sea. The seafloor falls away from every coast to as deep as 250 meters, and you can see the surface from above and below. Swim in open water: dive, surface, put on a burst of speed, climb out onto the shore and watch your breath. The deep has its own fog and light, weed, coral and schools of fish, its own creatures, and wrecks and sunken treasure under their guard.

credits.immersiveFootsteps.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, from the author’s MIT-licensed source, with the mod’s 210 sound clips.

credits.immersiveFootsteps.what.source: Footsteps that match the ground: grass, gravel, sand, mud, snow, stone paths and shallow or deep water outdoors, tile, stone or wood floors indoors, dungeon water, and leather, chain or plate boots on stone. Your armor rattles as you walk, and the mod adds its own landing and splash sounds. Comes in 2 sound qualities.

credits.kingsGambit.terms.source: Used with permission, on Mac’s word. The bundle names no author.

credits.kingsGambit.what.source: A battle of armies and kings, played at a tavern’s card table against the regulars, or online against another player. Its units use the Iliac Hand cards’ pictures, and its kings the Bay deck’s.

credits.l10n.bundled.source: Daggerfall’s original text is {pack}, used with its authors’ permission.

credits.l10n.checked.source: Machine translation by Claude, checked and corrected by {names}.

credits.l10n.machine.source: Machine translation by Claude, still being checked. Corrections from native speakers are welcome.

credits.layeredArmor.terms.source: Made for DFO and carried under the owner's exception for art drawn from Daggerfall's own (vendor/layered-armor/README.md).

credits.layeredArmor.what.source: The art of the Layered Gearing look: every helmet, chest and leg armor in leather, chain and plate of seven metals, and the cloaks and hoods, for both bodies, made for the game from Daggerfall's own class and enemy sprites.

credits.meanerMonsters.terms.source: Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar; Author: Hazelnut & Ralzar).

credits.meanerMonsters.what.source: Twenty monsters made tougher, with new damage, health, level and armor. Rats, bats and zombies are gentler. Werewolves and wereboars are a fifth larger, and the dragonling is two and a half times its size. Based on version 1.5.2. With the combat overhaul on, Kirk.O’s version of these numbers is used instead.

credits.oblivionLeveling.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license and names no author.

credits.oblivionLeveling.what.source: Another way to level, offered when you create a character. Raising skills fills a 100-point bar instead of Daggerfall’s skill total: primary and major skills fill it fastest, minor skills next and the rest slowest, and any overflow carries into the next level. Each level up gives you points to spend on a few attributes, with Luck costing more. You can set the points, how many attributes, and Luck’s cost on the mod’s tile. Originally an OpenMW Lua mod for Morrowind.

credits.oceanHoles.what.source: Blue holes in the deep. Far out in Iliac Puddle No More’s sea, the seafloor drops into a black pit under a plume of miasma. Swim down to reach a drowned, lightless dungeon where creatures of the deep replace the fire creatures, and loot is one material better.

credits.pcaao.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. Based on the released mod and its public source, which states no license.

credits.pcaao.what.source: The combat overhaul. Armor reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, and your skills and stats decide whether you hit. Weapons and armor wear by their kind and material, using his Believable Equipment Characteristics And Durability. Shields block by their material and your stats, critical hits multiply damage, and monsters have their own hides. His versions of Ralzar’s Meaner Monsters and of Roleplay & Realism’s archery apply when those mods are on.

credits.pixelifyGlyphs.terms.source: The game's own work (vendor/pixelify-glyphs/, built by tools/pixelifyGlyphs.py).

credits.pixelifyGlyphs.what.source: Two glyphs drawn for the enhanced skin on Pixelify Sans's own grid: a 2 and a Z that can no longer be taken for each other.

credits.raidingParties.terms.source: Made by Kamer for this game, used with his permission, with some bugs fixed.

credits.raidingParties.what.source: Raids on towns across Tamriel. Each day knights, bandits or orcs attack for 2 hours (10 real minutes online). Drive off 15 to 25 of them, with the town watch beside you, to free the town and raise your standing.

credits.raum.terms.source: The author’s own work, from his repository.

credits.raum.what.source: The book you read Daggerfall’s books in on the Enhanced skin: project-raum’s leather journal, with a cover that opens, two-page spreads, pages that turn, and torn, stained paper. The text is Daggerfall’s own, in its own fonts.

credits.rr.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License.

credits.rr.what.source: The mod’s rule changes: bows hit harder the longer you draw them, no climbing with a weapon out, swing speed from both speed and strength, smaller to-hit bonuses from materials, armor that wears from blows, the classic strength bonus, bank loans by level, ships boarded only from port towns, an encumbrance penalty, lights put out when you leave a dungeon by day, a purification potion that cures poison, varied looks for human enemies by class, expulsion from the Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood for poor work, hand-to-hand training at the Fighters Guild, and beds you can click to sleep in. Also its NPC variants, enhanced riding, refined training and the Master Armorer quests.

credits.rrItems.terms.source: Used with the authors’ permission under the MIT License. The 280 sprites are the authors’ own art.

credits.rrItems.what.source: Two new weapons, the Archer’s Axe and the Light Flail, and a light and a medium armor set in every metal, with their own inventory and paper-doll art. Also changes what items weigh and cost, and adds its loot tables, enemy gear, starting kits and shop stock.

credits.seasons.what.source: Autumn, spring and winter repaints of the trees, rocks and plants in woodland, hill, haunted and mountain areas. The textures are not included: they are read from your own copy of the mod.

credits.shieldWidget.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 600 sprites.

credits.shieldWidget.what.source: Shows your shield in first person, which the original game never did. It is drawn in its own metal and looks more battered as its condition drops. It slides away when you sheathe, swing or cast, bobs as you walk, raises and lowers, and rocks when a blow lands on it.

credits.silkscreen.terms.source: SIL Open Font License 1.1. The license is included with the glyph.

credits.silkscreen.what.source: The digit 5 in the Enhanced skin’s numbers. Pixelify Sans’s 5 looks like an 8, so this one digit comes from Silkscreen.

credits.spellIcons.what.source: Additional spell icons for the spell maker and spellbook.

credits.travelOptions.terms.source: Code under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut; PlayerAutoPilot Copyright (C) 2019 Jedidia). The 3 interface textures are the mod’s own art, used with the author’s permission.

credits.travelOptions.what.source: Travel across the land instead of arriving at once. The travel map lets you choose Daggerfall’s fast travel or a sped-up journey, with a panel to steer it, stops for encounters and places, and a key to follow Basic Roads’ roads and tracks. The travel map also gets a ports filter, a page with the road network drawn on it, a location info key and location markers. The autopilot is Jedidia’s, from Tedious Travel.

credits.unleveledLoot.terms.source: Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar).

credits.unleveledLoot.what.source: Loot and shop stock no longer scale with your level. Weapon and armor materials depend on your luck, the shop’s quality and the kind of dungeon. Gold on bodies is divided by your level and multiplied by your luck. Daedra and Orcs can drop their own metals, and any material can stand in for another.

credits.vorbis.terms.source: From vgmstream’s table (ISC-style license) and libvorbis’s encoder output (BSD-3-Clause, Xiph.org). Both licenses are included with the files.

credits.vorbis.what.source: Two Vorbis setup headers that Unity audio clips leave out. With them, Come Sail Away’s 5 sounds play exactly as the author made them.

credits.warmAshes.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission. The quests are his own, unchanged, and the ships are his edits applied to your own game files.

credits.warmAshes.what.source: Pirate ambushes at sea. Fast travel by ship can be attacked by pirates: you fight on your ship’s deck with your crew (on a borrowed ship if you own none), with the raiders’ ships nearby. Beat them and you land where you were headed. Includes his 4 quests and 6 ship layouts.

credits.weaponSheathing.terms.source: The mod’s own permission: free to use with credit and no fee.

credits.weaponSheathing.what.source: Sheathed Morrowind weapons stay on your body, at the hip or on the back in their own scabbards, with a quiver for a bow. Its 71 scabbard models and 3 skeleton add-ons are included and work as they do in OpenMW. The scabbards are by akortunov, Greatness7, Heinrich, London Rook, Lord Berandas, Melchior Dahrk, MementoMoritius, Petethegoat, PikachunoTM and Remiros, as the mod’s readme credits them.

credits.weaponWidget.what.source: Reworks the first-person weapon. Swings wind up from the idle pose and recover, the weapon shows in the hand you swing with, and sheathing slides it off the screen. Adds a walking bob, look inertia, stepped movement, double-size idle sprites from the mod, and recoil when you hit, parry or miss. The Morrowind arms move the same way.

credits.windmills.what.source: Windmills: the tower and its sails, the machinery inside with its turning gear and roller, 17 climate and season looks, and the 7 farms he chose for them. Enhanced skin only. The Classic skin shows Daggerfall’s own farms.

credits.worldOfDaggerfall.terms.source: Used with the author’s permission, confirmed by Mac.

credits.worldOfDaggerfall.what.source: The wilderness: his 65 layouts of bandit camps and forts, ruins, shrines, mountains and rock fields, listed at 227,938 places across the Iliac Bay, one to a map square, with the bandits, bears, warriors and treasure they hold. Also his camp outside Privateer’s Hold.

credits.worldTooltips.terms.source: Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (c) 2009-2018 jefetienne), with a second MIT notice for Daggerfall Workshop.

credits.worldTooltips.what.source: Shows a name under the crosshair for what you are looking at: a person, a shop sign and its opening hours, a door and its lock level, a dungeon entrance, a lever, a wheel, a ladder, a bookshelf, a summoned Daedra, and what a chest or a body holds. On the Enhanced skin it appears at the crosshair instead of in the mod’s tooltip panel.

crewHall.many.source: You have signed on as many sailors as one day allows. Come back tomorrow.

crewHall.unread.source: The crewmaster cannot check the roster now. Try again.

death.lineOnline.source: Your body falls. The world is not done with you yet.

decor.bar.keys.fly.source: walk keys, Jump up, Crouch down, Run faster

decor.bar.keys.flyTouch.source: the stick, and hold Fly up or Fly down

decor.bar.keys.lookTouch.source: drag: the piece stands where you look

decor.bar.keys.turn.source: wheel or Turn Left/Right (Shift for fine turns; turn a picture half round to flip it)

decor.draft.hallBoth.source: {pay} gold to confirm, {back} to the guild

decor.grants.busy.source: Someone else is using this chest.

decor.grants.noDrop.source: Shut the chest before you drop that.

decor.grants.whole.source: The chest takes the whole stack.

decor.strandedBack.source: {n, plural, one {One thing your home's chest had lost was found and put back in it.} other {# things your home's chests had lost were found and put back in them.}}

decor.tool.confirmFirst.source: Confirm or discard the changes first.

decor.tool.discardGaveBack.source: What the {name} held is back in your pack.

decor.tool.discardNotInPack.source: {name} is no longer in your pack, or is worn. Confirm takes its piece down.

decor.tool.keptShare.source: The room is kept. The guild has its share.

decor.tool.setAsideDown.source: {name} set aside. Confirm takes it down.

decor.tool.stationCleared.source: {name} is no longer a station. Confirm keeps it.

decor.tool.strayBack.source: {n, plural, one {One of your things was no longer here and went back to your pack.} other {# of your things were no longer here and went back to your pack.}}

decor.tool.unkeptRoom.source: The changes could not be kept.

decor.tool.unmarked.source: Take out what has no mark first.

decor.tool.unread.source: The room could not be read.

decor.yard.tooHighFree.source: Too high. Above {m} m, a decoration must stand on or against the building, no higher than its roof.

delve.brazier.drop.source: The flame falls. Take it up again.

delve.brazier.gutter.source: The flame goes out. Take another from the heart.

delve.brazier.take.source: You carry the flame. Your hands are full.

delve.brazier.won.source: Every brazier is lit. The vault is open.

delve.brazier.work.source: Carry the flame from the heart to the {n} braziers.

delve.hold.away.source: Go back into the circle. The ward fails when nobody holds it.

delve.hold.breath.source: The ward is quiet. Make ready.

delve.hold.failed.source: Nobody held the ward. It goes dark and its foes crumble.

delve.hold.gather.source: The ward wakes. Hold the circle.

delve.hold.outlasted.source: The captain outlasted the ward. It goes dark and its foes crumble.

delve.hold.won.source: The ward holds. The vault is open.

delve.litany.wake.source: The wrong plate wakes the guardians.

delve.litany.won.source: All the plates are lit. The vault is open.

delve.litany.work.source: Step on the plates in the same order.

delve.near.brazier.source: A flame burns at the heart of this floor, with cold braziers round it. Step inside to wake the rite.

delve.near.hold.source: An old ward is cut into this floor. Step inside it to wake it.

delve.near.litany.source: {k} plates are set in a ring in this floor. Step inside the ring to wake them.

delve.near.seals.source: Old seals are cut into this floor. Step inside the circle to raise them.

delve.near.springs.altar.source: {n} broken altars stand round this floor. Step inside the circle to wake them.

delve.near.springs.pool.source: {n} dark pools ring this floor. Step inside the circle to wake them.

delve.near.springs.tomb.source: {n} cracked tombs stand round this floor. Step inside the circle to wake them.

delve.near.vigil.source: A relic stands at the heart of this floor. Step inside the circle to wake it.

delve.near.weighing.source: Three plates are set in this floor, and stone weights lie by them. Step inside the circle to wake them.

delve.room.held.source: You hold another encounter here. Finish it or leave it first.

delve.seals.seals.source: Break the {n} seals before they sink.

delve.seals.sink.source: The seals sink. They rise again soon.

delve.seals.won.source: Every seal is broken. The vault is open.

delve.springs.outlasted.source: The sources outlasted the ward. It goes dark and its foes crumble.

delve.springs.spring.source: Foes pour from the sources. Break every source.

delve.springs.won.source: The sources are broken. The vault is open.

delve.vault.notYours.source: Only those who won this vault may open it.

delve.vault.sealedBrazier.source: Light the braziers to open it

delve.vault.sealedHold.source: Hold the ward to open it

delve.vault.sealedLitany.source: Light the plates to open it

delve.vault.sealedSeals.source: Break the seals to open it

delve.vault.sealedSprings.source: Break the sources to open it

delve.vault.sealedVigil.source: Keep the relic lit to open it

delve.vault.sealedWeighing.source: Hold the plates to open it

delve.vigil.breath.source: The relic's light steadies. Make ready.

delve.vigil.dark.source: The relic's light goes out. It wakes again in a minute.

delve.vigil.failed.source: Nobody kept the relic. It goes dark and its foes crumble.

delve.vigil.gather.source: The relic wakes. Keep its light.

delve.vigil.won.source: The relic's light holds. The vault is open.

delve.weighing.held.source: All three plates are held. Keep them held.

delve.weighing.take.source: You carry a stone weight. Your hands are full.

delve.weighing.won.source: The plates are held. The vault is open.

delve.weighing.work.source: Hold all three plates at once. Stand on a plate, or set a weight on it.

dex.troll.recovered.source: The {name} has recovered from its injuries.

dragon.aloft.source: It beats its wings and climbs back into the sky.

dragon.card.awayLine.source: Away. Call it, and it flies to your side.

dragon.card.brass.source: Brass and copper, made by the Dwemer.

dragon.card.comingLine.source: It is flying to your side.

dragon.card.foot.source: Your dragon waits where you leave it. Call it from anywhere outdoors, and it flies to your side.

dragon.card.waitingLine.source: Waiting where you left it, {far} m away.

dragon.care.ateOnTheRoad.source: {n, plural, one {Your dragon drank a flask of Dwarven Oil from your packs.} other {Your dragon drank # flasks of Dwarven Oil from your packs.}}

dragon.care.feedTip.source: A flask of Dwarven Oil, a day's food

dragon.care.noOil.source: You have no Dwarven Oil. A Stable sells it.

dragon.care.notHere.source: Your dragon is not here to feed.

dragon.care.rested.source: Your dragon has its breath back.

dragon.care.starving.source: Your dragon is too weak to gallop. Feed it Dwarven Oil.

dragon.care.winded.source: Your dragon is winded. It will not gallop or take off until it has its breath back.

dragon.care.windedLine.source: Winded. It will not gallop or take off until it has its breath back.

dragon.circles.source: A dragon circles in the sky {way}.

dragon.circles.shiny.source: A blue dragon circles in the sky {way}.

dragon.claim.bound.source: The Dwarven Dragon is yours. Ride it from the Transport window.

dragon.claim.guest.source: This dragon is not on your record yet: only registered accounts keep one. Add a username this week and it counts.

dragon.claim.recorded.source: The dragon's fall is on your record. Dragons slain: {n}.

dragon.claim.tamed.source: Its core still turns. The Dwarven Dragon is yours.

dragon.claim.tamedWaits.source: Its core still turns. The Dwarven Dragon is yours to ride after a later update.

dragon.gone.source: The dragon climbs away into the clouds.

dragon.grounded.source: It crashes down! Strike it while it is on the ground.

dragon.keep.aboard.source: Your dragon cannot land on a ship.

dragon.keep.alreadyAway.source: {name} is not here to send away.

dragon.keep.nameless.source: Your dragon has no name. Give it one.

dragon.keep.outdoors.source: You can only call your dragon outdoors.

dragon.no.far.source: Come closer to the dragon to fight it.

dragon.no.full.source: Too many fight this dragon already.

dragon.no.reload.source: Your game is out of date. Save, then reload or update the app to fight the dragon.

dragon.phase2.source: The dragon roars. Steam pours from its seams!

dragon.phase3.source: Its coil spins wild. Shrapnel falls from the sky!

dragon.spoils.granted.source: {name}'s hoard is yours. It is in your pack.

dragon.spoils.keptAnyone.source: The dragon's hoard waits for the one who fought it.

dragon.spoils.recovered.source: A dragon's hoard is in your pack.

effect.look.aetheric.source: Crystal shards rise off the ground and gather into a turning ring. It opens with a chime of its own.

effect.look.ashen.source: A foe you kill crumbles to ash from the feet up. Bone shards fall, and grey dust rolls out over the ground.

effect.look.automaton.source: Your horse wears riveted brass plates set with aetherium studs. Sparks fly off its hooves, and steam breathes from its chest.

effect.look.brass.source: A ring of brass cogs turns round a blue aetherium core. Steam vents at its foot.

effect.look.daedric.source: A jagged arch of black iron thrusts up round a crimson vortex. Its runes crawl, embers rise, and it opens in a burst.

effect.look.dawnfire.source: Your horse turns radiant gold, its legs burning up from the hooves. Its mane is golden fire, and its hoofprints burn.

effect.look.pyre.source: A Daedric sigil burns into the ground under the foe you kill. A pillar of crimson fire takes it, and embers storm upward.

effect.look.runic.source: Your portals turn ice-blue inside a ring of carved runes that glow as it turns.

effect.look.spectral.source: Your horse turns to a pale blue ghost that fades at the legs. Light wisps off it, and its hooves leave glowing prints.

effect.look.tonal.source: The foe you kill bursts into brass cogs and steam. A blue tonal ring rolls out over the ground.

effect.look.voidrend.source: A rift tears open in the foe you kill. Its shards spiral into the void, and the rift snaps shut in a ring of violet light.

effect.look.warhorse.source: Your horse turns black and crimson under scaled barding with burning edges. Its mane burns, and smoke and embers roll off its hooves.

eg.ask.bargain.source: One more decree this circle. Each member who says yes gains a Reliquary.

eg.ask.respite.source: The rest runs {min} minutes longer and the count holds.

eg.board.noRuns.source: No run is kept on this device yet.

eg.cmd.inside.source: In the breach: /breach pick N, vote yes|no|N, respite [no], cant N, tonic, buy cant|tonic|shard, surplus [reroll], use, bridge, annals [N], ping [danger|mine|cache], watch, bequest N, forsake, home, board.

eg.cmd.outside.source: Outside the breach: /breach answers your company's call, or opens the start window; /breach rehearse, /breach board, /breach annals [N].

eg.down.source: You are down. A party member can raise you within {s} seconds. Enter: give up.

eg.downOther.source: {name} is down. Raise them before they fall!

eg.fair.air.source: You stayed in the air longer than the Spire allows. Go back to the last island you stood on and cross again.

eg.fair.blind.source: The Spire lost sight of part of your crossing. Stay at the door - it opens for you once the Spire has seen you there.

eg.fair.speed.source: You crossed faster than the Spire allows. Go back to the last island you stood on and cross again.

eg.fair.void.source: You fell into the void. Go back to the last island you stood on and cross again.

eg.fall.raise.source: A party member can raise you. Enter: give up.

eg.key.shared.source: Every character on your account shares the same Weir Keys.

eg.objective.gauntlet.source: Silence each caster: stand on its plate, or slay it.

eg.panel.majority.source: The majority of those who answer decides.

eg.panel.noteKeys.source: 1-6 to choose, Y for Ready, R for a respite

eg.panel.noteTouch.source: Tap a card or a choice.

eg.panel.surplusCard.source: Spend a Surplus: a fourth card ({n} left)

eg.panel.surplusReroll.source: Spend a Surplus: draw new cards

eg.potion.wait.source: {kind, select, health {Health potion} magicka {Magicka potion} other {Potion}} {s} s

eg.progress.gauntlet.source: Casters left: {n}. Hold a plate {s} s or slay its caster

eg.start.rehearseFree.source: You can still rehearse Halls 1-5, free, once a day.

eg.start.stake.source: Opening the breach stakes one Weir Key.

eg.start.wagerRule.source: Up to three decrees, one from each family, for the whole breach. A wagered breach ranks on the Depths board only.

eg.vote.respiteHow.source: Answer a respite with R or /breach respite.

eg.vote.respiteNone.source: Nobody has asked for a respite.

enchant.soulGone.source: That soul is no longer in your pack.

ether.cross.passengers.source: Only your party can cross the Veil with you. The crossing waits until only your party is aboard.

events.board.more.source: {n, plural, one {1 more in Timers} other {# more in Timers}}

events.gate.live.source: It seals when this runs out

events.gate.soon.source: Its omen burns in the sky

events.serpent.live.source: It dives when this runs out

events.super.live.source: It fades away unbeaten when this runs out

features.armoryOthers.note.source: Whose Aura Armory pieces are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own pieces always show.

features.blood.effect.source: Takes effect at once; the number of marks that stay changes when the game next loads or you enter a dungeon.

features.blood.note.source: Stains stay on floors and walls where blood lands. A big killing blow sprays it further, and a heavy hit on you splashes a few drops on the screen. The slider sets how much, from Light to Abattoir; Off keeps the classic splash that fades away.

features.bowsLeftHand.effect.source: Takes effect on the next weapon you equip.

features.bowsLeftHand.note.source: Bows go in your left hand only, so you can keep a one-handed weapon in your right and switch between them. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.chooseGuildJobs.effect.source: Takes effect the next time a guild offers you work.

features.chooseGuildJobs.note.source: Guilds show you a list of the jobs you can take instead of giving you one at random. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.cloudQuality.note.source: How detailed the clouds in the enhanced outdoors are. Low is lighter on your machine; High looks best if you have power to spare.

features.combatVoices.note.source: You and your enemies grunt when swinging and cry out when hit. The sounds are in the original game but go unused. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.dungeonEncounters.note.source: Some dungeon rooms hold an encounter: a ward to hold against foes, sources or seals to break, or a puzzle to work out. Win one to open its vault. Online, your party wins it together.

features.dungeonMap3d.note.source: The enhanced map shows dungeons in 3D, hand-drawn: turn, tilt and zoom it, with every floor you’ve explored at its own height. Off shows one flat floor at a time.

features.dungeonWallStyle.note.source: Which textures dungeon walls use: Classic, the region’s climate (Climate) or random (Random). Climate and Random keep main-story dungeons classic; Climate Only and Random Only change them too. Classic by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.effect.gameLoads.source: Takes effect when the game next loads.

features.effect.nextDungeon.source: Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter.

features.effect.nextMap.source: Takes effect the next time a map is opened.

features.effect.worldLoads.source: Takes effect when the world next loads.

features.enemyInfighting.note.source: Monsters attack anything they aren’t allied with, not just you: a bear fights a spider, a Daedra fights a knight. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.enhancedAi.effect.source: Takes effect at once; pathfinding from the next dungeon you enter.

features.enhancedAi.note.source: Enemies take turns, back off when hurt, and archers keep their distance. Big attacks are marked on the ground: hit hard to stagger them or dodge. Red, hatched attacks can’t be stopped. Trees, rocks and crates block sight and missiles. Pathfinding works in dungeons only for now; towns, interiors and doors come later. Off keeps the classic behavior.

features.enhancedClimbing.note.source: Press Jump at a ledge to climb onto or over it, or while moving forward to vault a low wall. Jump at a high ledge to catch it and hang: Forward climbs up, Left and Right move along it, Crouch lets go. Hold Forward against any wall to climb it. Holding on wears out your grip; your Climbing skill sets how long it lasts, how high you reach and how fast you climb. Off keeps the classic climbing.

features.enhancedCombatVisuals.note.source: Hidden enemies can be seen: a chameleon shimmers, a shadow is a silhouette, and an invisible enemy flashes when you hit it. The rules don’t change. Off hides them as the original does.

features.enhancedEnvironments.note.source: A living sky with the sun, both moons and stars, clouds that build with the weather and cast shadows, falling rain and snow, and grass that bends in the wind. Off brings back the classic painted sky and weather. The third choice uses Dynamic Skies by BadLuckBurt and carademono, included with permission; its settings open on this tile.

features.enhancedLighting.effect.source: Lighting takes effect when the world next loads; steady shadows and calmer eye at once.

features.enhancedLighting.note.source: Warmer, more natural light: lanterns and torches that glow and fade with distance, light through fog, shadows from the sun and your torch, darker corners, a glow on windows and flames, and rays of sunlight. Off is the classic flat lighting. Steady shadows stops shadows flickering, at some cost to frame rate; Calmer eye slows how fast your eyes adjust to light and dark.

features.enhancedMap.note.source: One hand-drawn parchment map for the world, towns and dungeons, held in your hands, that you can pan and zoom. Off uses the classic three map windows.

features.enhancedWater.note.source: Seas, rivers and ponds you can see into: waves that grow with the wind, foam where they meet the shore, ripples where things move, the sky and the moon on the surface. Off brings back the classic flat water.

features.firstPersonLighting.note.source: What you hold in first person takes the light of where you stand: your weapon, your spellcasting hands, the torch in your off hand and the Morrowind arms.

features.grass.effect.source: The amount takes effect when the world next loads; the style at once.

features.grass.note.source: How much grass grows in the enhanced outdoors. Grass is the heaviest thing outdoors, so try Half first if the game runs slow. Meadow is hand-drawn tufts, flowers and bushes; Pixel is finer, older tufts; Smooth is soft, shaded blades.

features.groundSharpness.note.source: How sharp the ground looks into the distance. Off is the cheapest and blurs far ground; Maximum is the sharpest. Turn it down if the outdoors run slow.

features.killFxOthers.note.source: Whose kill effects and mount looks are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own always show.

features.kind.enhanced.blurb.source: This game’s own changes and additions to the original.

features.kind.mod.blurb.source: Mods by other authors, credited by name.

features.landViewDistance.note.source: How far the land around you is drawn, in map squares: up to 6 with the enhanced outdoors, and up to 4 on the classic UI or with the outdoors off.

features.livingAdventurers.note.source: Simulates rival adventurers delving dungeons across Tamriel, advancing, and leaving fallen remains.

features.livingBounties.note.source: Rebalances notice boards toward wilderness contracts with higher payouts that lower regional crisis tension.

features.livingCamps.note.source: Spawns slope-aligned roadside encampments, patrol outposts, and traveller tents along highways.

features.livingNaval.note.source: Populates open waters with multi-ship fleet skirmishes between provincial patrols and pirate squadrons.

features.livingNemesis.note.source: Dispatches persistent challengers, bounty hunters, and grudge avengers with roleplay dialogue checks.

features.livingPolitical.note.source: Drives regional state transitions between peace, war, plague, and civil strife across Tamriel.

features.livingQuarantine.note.source: Bars city gates around the clock during severe outbreaks and establishes outside relief tents.

features.livingRoadAdventurers.note.source: Spawns non-hostile adventurers travelling highways, camping in the wilds, returning with dungeon spoils, or fighting monsters along the road.

features.livingTravel.note.source: Allows journeys and fast travel to be interrupted by roadside caravans, dilemmas, or hostile ambushes.

features.livingUrban.note.source: Generates contained street clashes between the city watch and insurgents during regional war and strife.

features.lootRarity.effect.source: Takes effect on the next drop; items you wear update within a few seconds.

features.lootRarity.note.source: Weapons, armor and jewelry can drop as Magic, Rare or Legendary, with extra bonuses you can read and compare. The odds depend on what you killed, where, and your luck. Rare and Legendary gear is rarer early on and becomes more common as you grow. Rare and Legendary items drop unidentified. Off is the classic loot. Online, some weapons carry a sigil that grows with your Renown.

features.mod.beautifulTowns.effect.source: Takes effect the next time you start the game; loading a save is not enough. Offline it also needs Replace Game Artwork.

features.mod.betterAmbience.effect.source: Takes effect at once; a dungeon’s fog and light from the next one you enter.

features.mod.climatesCalories.effect.source: Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.

features.mod.climatesCalories.note.source: Hunger, thirst, sleep and the weather come into play: eat, drink, dress for the climate and rest by a campfire or in a bed. On Boons neglect costs nothing, and staying fed, watered and rested in a bed or by a fire gives bonuses; on Casual, unmet needs only drain some stamina (never more than half) and it comes back once you’ve seen to them; on Hard they cost attributes and health and can make you sick; Off is the classic game.

features.mod.diverseWeapons.effect.source: Takes effect when a weapon is next drawn.

features.mod.eyeOfTheBeholder.effect.source: Takes effect at once. Scroll out to leave first person.

features.mod.foraging.effect.source: Takes effect at once; its quests when the game next loads.

features.mod.immersiveTravel.effect.source: Takes effect the next time you start the game; loading a save is not enough. Fares and rules change at the next map.

features.mod.kingsGambit.note.source: A game of armies and kings at a tavern's card table, against a regular or another player, for gold or for fun. Off, the tables offer only Hold'em and Iliac Hand.

features.mod.oblivionRemasterLeveling.ef.source: Takes effect on the next character you make; a character keeps the system they were created with.

features.mod.physicalItems.effect.source: Takes effect at once; a size change applies to items that drop after it.

features.mod.projectLegacy.effect.source: Takes effect at once; a family keeps the model it was founded with.

features.mod.unleveledLoot.effect.source: Takes effect on the next drop or shop restock.

features.mod.warmAshesShips.effect.source: Takes effect on your next sea voyage.

features.mod.weaponSheathing.effect.source: Takes effect at once with the Morrowind body.

features.mod.weaponSheathing.note.source: With the Morrowind body, a put-away weapon hangs in a scabbard on your hip or back, and a bow gets a quiver. Off, a put-away weapon disappears, as in Morrowind.

features.mod.windmillsKamer.note.source: Windmills with turning sails on seven farms, with machinery inside and a look for every climate and season. Off leaves the farms as they were.

features.moddedLighting.note.source: Needs the Improved Interior Lighting mod. Its warm, flickering lights replace the classic lighting, and with shadows on, lamps, people and monsters cast soft shadows too.

features.mwItemIcons.note.source: With Morrowind data, items in your inventory and quickslots are shown as rendered 3D ground meshes. Off shows classic 2D item sprites.

features.mwModelDetail.note.source: With the Morrowind body, Pixelated draws bodies, horses and your arms in large pixels like the classic sprites. Sharp draws them at your screen’s full resolution and uses more video memory.

features.mwPlayerBody.note.source: With Morrowind data, your character is drawn in 3D: hands and weapons in first person, full body in third person, and a 3D figure in the inventory. Off keeps classic 2D sprites and the paperdoll.

features.navalCombat.effect.source: Takes effect at once; Ship handling, the next time you take the helm. Online it is always on.

features.navalCombat.note.source: Ship battles on Come Sail Away’s boats: look to one side and hold Attack to aim a broadside, then let go to fire. Pirates, merchants and navies sail every sea. Board a ship that surrenders. Piracy is a crime.

features.nearDeathWarning.note.source: The screen pulses as your health gets low: slowly below 40%, fast below 20%. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.offlineFirmament.note.source: Enables the Firmament constellation passive tree and Renown progression while playing offline.

features.offlineHousing.note.source: Buy and sell homes at the front door across all towns and hamlets, as in online DFO. Off restores classic bank housing.

features.offlineProfessions.note.source: Enables gathering nodes (mining, herbs, logging, hunting, fishing) and crafting professions offline.

features.questHerald.note.source: A notice slides in when a quest begins, when its journal gains an entry, when one of its deadlines is less than a day away, and when it ends. Off updates the journal without a notice.

features.questMarks.note.source: Places your quests send you to are marked on the map once your map knows them, and the quest you follow is marked on the compass. Off is the classic map and compass, which mark nothing for a quest.

features.questTracker.note.source: A card at the top right shows the quest you track from the journal, or else the one it last updated: its newest entry, where it points and the time left. Off keeps the classic screen, with no quest card.

features.questlines.effect.source: Takes effect on the next quest you take; quests you already have keep the rules they began with.

features.questlines.note.source: Every quest shows its objectives, some let you choose how they end, some offer a piece of gear fitted to you when done, and questlines lead to the Breaches, the Battlespire and the Abyss. Off is the classic journal and its rewards, and online it is always on.

features.quickLoot.note.source: Loot without opening a window: the mouse wheel moves through the list, Activate takes one item, and the Take everything key takes all but junk (Take gear sets which gear). Off uses the inventory window.

features.quickSlots.note.source: Diamond puts 4 slots in a diamond at the bottom left, on keys 1 to 4. Hotbar puts 10 above your health bars on keys 1 to 0; Diamonds makes them diamonds. Drag an item or spell onto a slot, or point at it and press the key. Off hides them, but their keys still work.

features.realForests.note.source: Trees grow together in forests, with open grassland between them. Dungeons, ruins, shrines and camps are often hidden in the woods, and towns and farms stand in cleared fields. Deserts are unchanged. Off spreads the trees evenly, like the original.

features.renderScale.note.source: Draws the world at a lower resolution and scales it up to fit; menus and the HUD stay sharp. Try 75% if the outdoors run slow on a big or high-resolution screen. Retro Picture Mode replaces this while it is on.

features.resourceHighlights.note.source: How herbs, veins, trees and other gathering spots near you stand out. Glint makes them catch the light with sparkles; Outline rings each one in its profession’s color, plain to see day or night; Both does both.

features.smallerDungeons.effect.source: Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter. A save made at the other size puts you at the dungeon’s start.

features.smallerDungeons.note.source: Dungeons bigger than five blocks are cut down to five: a center block with four around it, the same every visit. Main-story dungeons keep full size; a quest keeps the size it was set up at. Online every dungeon has its own size instead.

features.torchesFromItems.effect.source: Takes effect at once; new characters and shop stock follow it.

features.torchesFromItems.note.source: Your light in dungeons comes from a torch, lantern or candle you carry, and it burns down, instead of a light you always have. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.townWatch.note.source: When a monster attacks you in a town and you’re not wanted, the town guard comes to help, then leaves once it’s safe. Commit a crime and they come for you as usual. Off keeps the classic guard, which only shows up for crimes.

features.variedDungeonMonsters.note.source: Random monsters are picked from the dungeon’s full list around your level, so a dungeon has more variety instead of the same few. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.waterQuality.note.source: How detailed the enhanced water is. Full shows what lies under the surface and ripples where things move; Simple is lighter on your machine.

features.weatherEvents.note.source: Rain, storms and snow move across the land with the wind, so you can see a storm coming, walk into it and out the other side. Off uses the classic weather, the same everywhere in the region.

features.wetWorld.note.source: After rain the ground darkens and puddles shine. Wet is sheen and ripples; Full also mirrors buildings in them. Off stays dry.

features.wildernessCamps.note.source: Out in the wilds you sometimes meet a small group of enemies, a camp or a roaming pack, instead of only one at a time. Off keeps the classic single encounters.

features.wildlife.note.source: Birds, bats and small animals live outdoors. Flocks cross the sky, birds sit on roofs and fly off as you come near, and small animals run from your feet.

features.wind.note.source: See the wind in the enhanced outdoors: trees and plants lean and sway with it, and faint streaks of air show which way it blows and how hard.

festival.offering.tookIn.source: You take in your offering. +{n, plural, one {# Soul Cake} other {# Soul Cakes}}

festival.refusal.count.source: You hold fewer than that now.

festival.refusal.held.source: Your account does not hold that.

festival.refusal.taken.source: You already took a cake here today.

festival.refusal.ware.source: The Wyrd Sister has no such thing.

festival.window.cardsSub.source: Festival cards. Never in a pack.

festival.window.earnGiven.source: Earned when others take Soul Cakes from your offerings.

festival.window.earnStarwarden.source: Earned on The Thirteenth of Frostfall.

festival.window.earnTaken.source: Earned by taking Soul Cakes from others' offerings.

festival.window.kept.source: One per account, kept for good.

festival.window.offeringSub.source: Set it out at your own door.

festival.window.raimentSub.source: An Aetheric set of nine. Bound to you.

festival.window.whatAura.source: A ring of witchfire and candles at your feet.

festival.window.whatIcon.source: Shown in your portrait in place of your face.

festival.window.whatTitle.source: Worn over your name, for every player to see.

firmament.build.loaded.source: Build loaded. Press {accept} to keep it.

firmament.build.loadedCost.source: Build loaded. Press {accept} to keep it. Removing the stars it leaves out costs {silver} silver.

firmament.build.noSign.source: That build has no valid birthsign.

firmament.build.oldSky.source: That code is from a different version of the Firmament. Ask for a new code.

firmament.build.path.source: That build has a star that isn't connected to its birthsign.

firmament.build.pointsCraft.source: That build needs {need, plural, one {# Star} other {# Stars}} and up to {life, plural, one {# Craft point} other {# Craft points}}. You have {stars, plural, one {# Star} other {# Stars}} and {craft, plural, one {# Craft point} other {# Craft points}}.

firmament.confirm.removeCost.source: Remove {n, plural, one {# star} other {# stars}} for {silver} silver.

firmament.confirm.removeFree.source: Remove {n, plural, one {# star} other {# stars}} for free.

firmament.hint.source: Click a star to learn it and the stars on the way · Right-click a learned star to remove it · Drag to pan · Scroll to zoom · F: center on your birthsign

firmament.hintTouch.source: Tap a star to see it, tap again to learn it and the stars on the way · Hold a learned star to remove it · Drag to pan · Pinch to zoom

firmament.no.otherSign.source: You already have a birthsign. To change it, right-click yours to reset all stars.

firmament.no.path.source: Your stars have no path to this star.

firmament.no.points.source: You need {need} {need, plural, one {point} other {points}} and have {have}.

firmament.no.signFirst.source: Choose a birthsign first: one of the seven large stars.

firmament.no.stars.source: You need {need} {need, plural, one {Star} other {Stars}} and have {have}. Craft points can only be spent on craft stars.

firmament.purse.craftTip.source: Craft points: 1 for every 8 ranks, counting all your professions. They can only be spent on craft stars (the outer ring).

firmament.purse.starsTip.source: Stars: 2 for each Renown level after the first (your Renown is {renown}). They can be spent on any star.

firmament.refusal.closed.source: The Firmament isn't available to you right now.

firmament.refusal.key.source: One of those stars is unknown.

firmament.refusal.offline.source: The server didn't answer. Your change is saved and will be sent again.

firmament.refusal.path.source: A star isn't connected to your birthsign.

firmament.refusal.rate.source: Too many changes this hour. Try again later.

firmament.refusal.respecLost.source: The server didn't answer the respec. Open the Firmament again in a moment to see if it went through.

living.adventurer.duelLost.source: Yield! Better luck next time, wanderer. The gold stays with me.

living.adventurer.duelWon.source: A well-fought contest! You have earned my respect and the wager.

living.adventurer.enviousTaunt.source: Another strutting 'hero' thinking they own Tamriel. Step aside before I make you!

living.adventurer.questIntercepted.source: A rival adventurer cleared the dungeon ahead of you and claimed the objective!

living.adventurer.reclaimFailed.source: The rival adventurer refused to yield the prize and walked away.

living.adventurer.reclaimSuccess.source: You have successfully recovered the quest objective from your rival!

living.checkpoint.halt.source: Halt! State your business at this military checkpoint.

living.checkpoint.knightPass.source: Hail, noble Knight! The road is yours; pass freely.

living.checkpoint.passed.source: Papers are in order. Move along, traveller.

living.checkpoint.refused.source: Halt! You shall not pass without authorization!

living.checkpoint.tollDemand.source: Wartime transit requires an inspection toll of {gold} gold.

living.crisis.entry.famine.source: Gaunt townsfolk line the streets of {town}. Famine grips the region.

living.crisis.entry.plague.source: Fever warnings hang at the gates of {town}. Plague stalks the region.

living.crisis.entry.strife.source: Armed patrols march through {town} amid civil strife.

living.crisis.entry.war.source: {town} is under martial law as war rages across the region.

living.economy.famineFood.source: Grain is scarce and provisions fetch a heavy price this season.

living.economy.plaguePotions.source: Remedies and alchemy ingredients are in high demand due to the plague.

living.economy.warShortage.source: Weapons and armor are in short supply due to the ongoing conflict.

living.naval.battleNotice.source: A naval skirmish rages between patrol ships and pirates!

living.nemesis.approach.source: A grim hunter confronts you, holding a contract with your name.

living.nemesis.bribe.source: Gold speaks louder than blood today. Watch your back.

living.nemesis.honor.source: Honor prevails today; our paths may cross again under fairer stars.

living.nemesis.intimidated.source: The challenger shrinks back before your grim gaze and reconsiders their life choices.

living.nemesis.motive.arcane.source: Such powerful artifacts belong in the hands of a master, not an ignorant amateur!

living.nemesis.motive.assassin.source: The Dark Brotherhood sends its regards. You were marked for death.

living.nemesis.motive.bounty.source: There is a fat bounty on your head, criminal. Dead or alive, I collect!

living.nemesis.motive.glory.source: They say you are the fiercest warrior in the land. Let us see if you bleed like one!

living.nemesis.motive.grudge.source: Remember me?! You humiliated me, and now I have returned to pay the blood debt!

living.nemesis.motive.marauder.source: Drop your weapons and empty your purse, traveler! Every coin or your life!

living.nemesis.tauntSuccess.source: The rival sneers and waves their retinue back: 'Stay out of this, fools! This dog is mine alone!'

living.plea.escort.source: The roads crawl with bandits. Might an able blade walk with me to the next crossroads?

living.plea.famine.source: Alms, kind stranger! The granaries are empty and my children weep from hunger. Spare a coin for bread?

living.plea.helped.source: Blessings of the Divines upon you! Tamriel still knows true virtue.

living.plea.parted.source: May Stendarr watch over your journey nonetheless.

living.plea.plague.source: Merciful traveler! My kin is burning with the plague fever. Do you have a healing remedy to spare?

living.plea.rebuffed.source: Curse your cold heart! May misfortune dog your footsteps!

living.plea.war.source: The village was put to the torch by marauders! Please, help us with passage far from this bloodshed!

living.quarantine.gateClosed.source: The city gates are barred due to an outbreak of plague.

living.quarantine.reliefTent.source: A relief healer tent stands outside the locked walls.

living.roadAdv.camp.source: {name} tends a roadside campfire: "Rest your feet by the embers, traveler, if you come in peace."

living.roadAdv.declined.source: "I walk my own path today, wanderer. Perhaps when your purse or renown is heavier."

living.roadAdv.extorted.source: {name} backs down with a scowl and tosses you a pouch of dungeon spoils.

living.roadAdv.intelShared.source: You exchange maps and road warnings over the fire, feeling refreshed for the journey ahead.

living.roadAdv.optionExtort.source: Intimidate (Streetwise): demand a share of their dungeon spoils.

living.roadAdv.optionIntel.source: Trade road news, dungeon intel, and share the camp.

living.roadAdv.optionRecruit.source: Invite to travel and fight alongside you ({gold}g retainer or Etiquette).

living.roadAdv.optionSpar.source: Propose a friendly wager match of blades ({gold}g).

living.roadAdv.parted.source: You exchange a respectful nod and continue along the road.

living.roadAdv.recruited.source: {name} salutes and falls in beside you: "My blade is with you along this road!"

living.roadAdv.skirmish.source: {name} wipes blood from their blade: "Well met! These beasts nearly had the drop on me!"

living.roadAdv.spoils.source: {name} guards a heavy chest of dungeon spoils: "Cleared the crypt ahead. A profitable day for bold steel!"

living.roadAdv.traveling.source: {name} nods along the highway: "Bound for the next delve. Keep your steel sharp on these roads."

living.rumor.famineEnd.source: Relief caravans have reached {region}, easing the famine at last.

living.rumor.famineMid.source: Severe famine starves {region}! Granaries are empty and desperate beggars plead for coin on every road.

living.rumor.famineStart.source: Blighted harvests in {region} have driven up the cost of grain and tavern meals.

living.rumor.plagueEnd.source: The worst of the plague in {region} has passed, and the quarantine cordons are finally lifting.

living.rumor.plagueMid.source: Plague has locked the city gates of {region} under strict quarantine! Only relief tents stand outside.

living.rumor.plagueStart.source: Healers warn of a dark fever spreading through {region}. Best stock up on potions.

living.rumor.strifeEnd.source: The city watch has quelled the worst of the uprising in {region}.

living.rumor.strifeMid.source: Insurgents clash openly with the city watch across {region}!

living.rumor.strifeStart.source: Angry mobs and agitators stir unrest in the streets of {region}.

living.rumor.warEnd.source: A fragile truce holds in {region}, though bands of deserters still roam the highways.

living.rumor.warMid.source: Open war engulfs {region}! Soldiers inspect travelers at road checkpoints and blades cost a fortune.

living.rumor.warStart.source: Scouts report border clashes in {region}. Smiths are already raising prices on steel.

living.travel.ambush.source: You are ambushed along the road!

living.travel.caravan.source: A traveling caravan has made camp along the road.

living.travel.dilemma.source: A stranded traveler waves for assistance.

living.travel.stealthEvadeOption.source: Slip past the ambush undetected through the brush (Stealth).

living.travel.stealthEvaded.source: You slip silently around the highwaymen without a sound.

living.travel.stealthSpotted.source: Your keen stealth spots highwaymen lying in ambush ahead before they notice you!

living.travel.stealthSurpriseOption.source: Strike first from the shadows! (Surprise bonus)

living.urban.orderRestored.source: The guards have restored order in the district.

living.urban.skirmishStart.source: A skirmish erupts in the streets! Townsfolk flee for cover.

livingWorld.friend.court.source: {name} counts you a friend now. You can court them: ask about Courtship under Tell me about.

lock.act.autoWhy.source: Roll your chance to open the lock. A failed roll snaps a pick.

lock.need.source: You need a lockpick to pick this lock.

lock.window.gentle.source: Gentle work is on, so the pins need no timing. Auto attempt rolls your chance. A failed roll snaps a pick.

lock.window.gentlePress.source: Gentle work is on, so the pins are not lifted one by one. Use Auto attempt.

lock.window.keys.source: Left and Right or 1-{n}: choose a pin. Space, Up, W, Enter or a click: lift and set. Q: auto attempt. Esc: leave.

lock.window.start.source: Lift the pins one at a time. The binding pin rises slowly and waits at the line. Press again while it waits to set it.

lock.word.break.source: {count, plural, one {Your lockpick snaps! # left.} other {Your lockpick snaps! # left.}}

lock.word.falseSet.source: A false set. That pin is a spool, cut narrow so it catches early. Lift it and set it again.

lock.word.lift.source: This pin is binding. Press again while it waits at the line.

lock.word.open.source: The plug turns. The lock is open.

lock.word.slip.source: Your pick slips, and a pin drops back.

lock.word.springy.source: That pin springs straight back. It is not binding yet.

lockpick.item.use.source: In Steal mode, activate a locked door, chest or crate to pick it. A pick can snap.

lockpick.item.useLine.source: Switch to Steal mode and activate a locked door, chest or crate to pick its lock.

lockpick.item.what.source: A thin steel pick and a tension wrench, for locks that are not yours.

loot.room.lapsed.source: That take was not confirmed in time, so the item is back where it was.

loot.room.skew.source: Another player here is on a different version of the game, so this can't be opened until you are both on the same one.

lw.cutpurse.0.1.source: My purse! Thief! Stop that thief!

lw.cutpurse.chase.0.0.source: Stop, thief! In the Emperor's name!

lw.cutpurse.chase.0.2.source: Give it back. Now go, and stay off my street.

lw.cutpurse.chase.1.2.source: Back to its owner, that purse.

lw.dice.2.1.source: The gods hate you tonight, friend.

lw.dice.2.2.source: The gods and my creditors both.

lw.flirt.0.1.source: Do I? You've had a cup or two.

lw.flirt.1.1.source: Ask me again when you've washed.

lw.flirt.2.0.source: I saved you the last of the honey cake.

lw.flirt.2.1.source: Did you now. Well. Sit, then.

lw.news.cry.1.source: Letters for {place}! A coin a letter!

lw.news.cry.2.source: Hear ye, people of {town}! The roads are open!

lw.sermon.0.0.source: Hear me, people of {town}! The Eight watch over all who do right!

lw.sermon.0.1.source: Give alms, keep faith, and fear nothing!

lw.sermon.1.0.source: Repent! The gods see every crooked scale in {town}!

lw.sermon.2.1.source: Remember my debts, while you're at it.

lw.watch.beggar.0.0.source: Keep out of the way of the carts, you.

lw.watch.beggar.1.1.source: None, officer. The gods keep you.

lw.watch.beggar.2.2.source: Not a word of it to the others.

lw.watch.buy.0.0.source: One of those, if it's warm.

lw.watch.buy.1.1.source: The same as yesterday, and cheaper.

lw.watch.buy.2.0.source: An apple for a hungry man on duty?

lw.watch.buy.2.1.source: Here. Keep the cutpurses off my stall.

lw.watch.moveAlong.0.0.source: Move along, you. Not in front of the shops.

lw.watch.moveAlong.2.0.source: On your feet. The magistrate comes through today.

lw.watch.word.0.1.source: Quiet enough. The dogs kept me up.

lw.watch.word.1.1.source: Well enough. My roof leaks again.

lw.watch.word.1.2.source: Not a matter for the watch, that.

lw.watch.word.4.1.source: Somebody has to be. You, for one.

lw.watch.word.5.1.source: With you on the street? I'll sleep sound.

madeRules.avoidDeath.source: Stendarr's mercy does not reach here.

madeRules.castOut.source: A death casts you out before the gate.

madeRules.fallDown.source: A death lays you down for {s} seconds: a party member can raise you there. Past it, you fall.

madeRules.finalIn.source: A death is final for this Abyss Dungeon - unless a party member raises you within {s} seconds.

madeRules.noMarkRecall.source: Mark and Recall do not work here.

madeRules.noPenalty.source: A death costs you no gold.

madeRules.potionClock.source: Each kind of potion waits {s} seconds after the last one.

madeRules.regen.source: Regeneration heals at half strength, and not at all for {s} seconds after you are hurt.

madeRules.regenTip.source: Restores health every round - held here: half, and none for {s} seconds after you are hurt.

madeRules.techFlight.source: A weapon technique cannot carry you over a gap.

madeRules.unstuckHome.source: /unstuck takes you out by the way home.
