menu.online.balanceNote.source: Set for everyone online, so no setting makes one character stronger or richer than the rest. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.carriageNote.source: Set for everyone online. Carriages wait at every city gate, trips on the travel map are traveled in full, and a driver’s fare is your fast travel over land, at the same price for everyone. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.groundNote.source: Set for everyone online, because everyone has to stand on the same ground: roads, rivers, camp sites and the seafloor. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.lockNote.source: Always on online: the shared world uses every enhancement. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.modsNote.source: Most mods are your choice online. A few are set for everyone, so all players share the same ground and rules. Ground: Basic Roads, World of Daggerfall, Iliac Puddle No More’s sea and depth, and There’s a Hole in the Bottom of the Ocean. Rules: every setting of Meaner Monsters, the Combat and Armor Overhaul, Unleveled Loot, Roleplay & Realism, Roleplay & Realism: Items and Oblivion leveling, except who stands behind shop counters and which leveling your character uses. Travel Options is on for everyone, so every trip over land is traveled and ships sail only from ports. Immersive Travel is on for everyone too: carriages wait at every city gate, a driver’s fare is your fast travel over land, and fares are the same for everyone. Its map style stays your choice.

menu.online.needsAccount.source: Online needs an account, so no one else can use your name. Playing as a guest takes one click and no email.

menu.online.noSaves.source: Each offline character can be brought online from here, once.

menu.online.rules.source: Everyone plays their own save, and you can see and talk to each other anywhere. Dungeons and buildings are shared: enemies, doors, levers and opened chests are the same for everyone and stay that way. In towns and the wilds, everyone nearby sees the same monsters and can fight them, and they can hurt you too. {skyDay} The world’s clock and sky run on real time. Resting, travel, jail and training don’t move them, so a quest waiting for a time of day waits for the world’s, and a lycanthrope’s full moon lasts one night. Your character also has their own clock. It runs while you play and stops while you are logged off. Resting, travel, jail and training use it. Your wounds, spells, hunger, diseases, curses, guild ranks, rented rooms, loans and repairs run on it. Quest timers run on the world’s clock while you play. Resting, waiting and traveling don’t use up a quest’s days, and time logged off never counts. A quest that only asks you to wait, like a letter or “come back in a few days”, moves on after a couple of minutes of play. Rest at a fire, a tent or a bed: a night passes at once, at most once every 10 minutes of play, and party members within 15 meters sleep with you. Every enhancement is on for everyone, but your interface is your own. Most mods stay your choice online. A few are set for everyone: those that change the ground, monsters, loot or the rules. The Mods page marks each one.

menu.online.rulesetNote.source: Set for everyone online, so all players share one set of combat, training and swimming rules. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.settingNote.source: Set for everyone online, so enchanted items are repaired the same way for all players. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.sharedNote.source: On for everyone online, because a dungeon’s monsters belong to whoever hosts it and loot passes between players. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.signIn.source: Sign in or continue as guest

menu.online.skyDay.source: A day in the world is an hour of real time: {onHour, select, yes {midnight falls on the hour} other {midnight falls at {midnight}}}, and dusk at {dusk}.

menu.online.skyDayUntil.source: A day in the world is two hours of real time until {turn}; from then on it is an hour: {onHour, select, yes {midnight falls on the hour} other {midnight falls at {midnight}}}, and dusk at {dusk}.

menu.online.travelNote.source: On for everyone online: every trip over land is traveled, and ships sail only from ports. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.online.worldEventNote.source: On for everyone online: a raid is shared, so everyone in town fights the same raiders and every kill counts for all. Offline, your own choice applies.

menu.ovh.custom.source: Custom: your own mix from Settings. Using a look sets every switch it covers.

menu.packs.blurb.source: Your own music, sounds and texture packs (.dfmod), kept in this browser.

menu.packs.detailNote.source: Texture detail: {detail}. Higher is sharper but uses more memory and loads slower. “full” can run out of memory with HD packs. Applies to areas loaded afterwards.

menu.packs.dfmodsBlurb.source: Daggerfall Unity texture mods, such as DREAM. Pick one or more .dfmod files. Mod scripts don’t run. Vanilla Enhanced comes with the game, and a copy you attach is used instead of the built-in one.

menu.packs.inBundleOff.source: {n} textures in the bundle · switched off

menu.packs.indexing.source: Reading. It joins the load order when done.

menu.packs.lightingBlurb.source: Improved Interior Lighting: warm lights in buildings and dungeons. Pick its .dfmod, then turn it on in {path}.

menu.packs.loadOrder.source: In load order: where two mods carry the same texture, the later one is drawn. A mod always loads after the mods it is built on.

menu.packs.nomods.source: Not loaded: this page was opened with ?nomods.

menu.packs.removeAllDfmodsBody.source: This clears every attached .dfmod texture mod from this browser; the built-in ones stay. It takes full effect the next time an area loads.

menu.packs.removeLightingBody.source: This clears {mod} from this browser; the lighting goes back to what it was.

menu.packs.removeModBody.source: This clears {mod} from this browser. It takes full effect the next time an area loads.

menu.packs.removeMusicBody.source: This clears your music files from this browser; the original game’s own songs play again. A sound pack stays.

menu.packs.removeSoundBody.source: This clears your sound files from this browser; the original game’s own sounds play again. A music pack stays.

menu.packs.removeTextureBody.source: This clears the texture folder you picked from this browser. Attached .dfmod texture mods stay. It takes full effect the next time an area loads.

menu.packs.shippedOff.source: Ships with the game · {n} textures · switched off

menu.packs.supplied.source: Music files supplied: {music} · Texture files supplied: {textures} · Sound files supplied: {sounds}

menu.packs.textureModsBuiltIn.source: {n} attached · {builtIn} built in · {inUse} textures in use

menu.packs.twoVersions.source: Two versions of the same mod are attached (for example DREAM and DREAM 90s). Only one shows for each texture, but both use memory. Remove one.

menu.peers.attackNote.source: Hear other players’ weapon swings, and their tools as they gather.

menu.peers.blurb.source: Players without a Morrowind body show as their chosen sprite, or their class.

menu.peers.crowdNote.source: How many other players are drawn at once, the nearest first. Your party, your duel opponent and anyone you trade, ride or sail with always show. The count is off in a PvP zone, a siege, a Royal Tourney and the Arena, but not in the Burning Court.

menu.peers.rangeNote.source: How far away other players are drawn. Your party and your duel opponent always show. Shorter runs faster, but 150 m can hide an archer.

menu.peers.restNote.source: Sleep when a party member within 15 m sleeps at a fire, a tent or a bed.

menu.peers.show.source: Show me to travelers in my region

menu.peers.showNote.source: Outdoors, players in your region see you on the overworld and the map. Nothing is shared from indoors except with your party. Kept on this device.

menu.peers.spellsNote.source: Let players outside your party cast healing and protective spells on you.

menu.peers.spriteNote.source: On: the sprite above. Off: the paperdoll.

menu.peers.yardsNote.source: How far away other players’ yard decorations are drawn. Your own yard always shows. Nearer is faster in busy towns.

menu.questRepair.ask.source: Restores missing quest people, items, foes and map marks. Progress is kept.

menu.questRepair.away.source: In a game: open Settings from the pause menu.

menu.questRepair.failed.source: The repair could not run here.

menu.questRepair.note.source: Restores missing quest people, items, foes and map marks. Progress is kept.

menu.realm.broughtIn.source: {name} is online now. Play them from the list above.

menu.realm.copied.source: {name} is copied as a new offline character. Nothing you play on the copy comes back online.

menu.realm.deleteBody.source: Deleting an online character is permanent. Its Renown, professions, Stores, the homes it bought and its guild place are lost. Homes belong to your account, so your other characters lose them too. Any offline copy you made stays.

menu.realm.none.source: No online characters yet. Make one, or bring one of yours in below.

menu.realm.undoBody.source: {name} didn’t finish coming online because its first save never arrived. Undo removes it and gives back its home and guild place, so you can bring the offline character online again. To finish instead, click Bring online on it below.

menu.realm.undone.source: {name} is no longer online. Its home and guild place are back with the offline character. Bring it online again when you are ready.

menu.save.agoDays.source: {n, plural, one {# day ago} other {# days ago}}

menu.save.agoHours.source: {n, plural, one {# hour ago} other {# hours ago}}

menu.save.agoMinutes.source: {n, plural, one {# minute ago} other {# minutes ago}}

menu.save.notHereWhy.source: You can’t save here. Step back outside to save again.

menu.settings.preset.effect.source: Steady shadows and the windows change at once; the rest when the world next loads.

menu.settings.preset.note.source: View distance, grass, clouds, ground sharpness, water, wet ground, windows and steady shadows.

menu.settings.resetBody.source: Every setting and mod goes back to its default. Your interface, text size and key bindings are kept.

menu.settings.restoreTabBody.source: Every option on this tab goes back to its default.

menu.settings.storedBlurb.source: Kept in your settings file, but not used yet.

menu.settings.tip.frameCap.source: The most frames a second the game draws. Off lets your screen set the pace. In the desktop app with Wait For Screen Refresh off, Off still holds the game at {max} frames a second.

menu.settings.unavailableBlurb.source: Fixed by the browser or by this game. Each row says what you get instead.

menu.shop.hideNote.source: Take the shop off the pause screen. Your Aurum and your items stay on your account.

menu.skipVideo.note.source: Open straight onto the main menu. Applies next launch.

menu.spire.fill.note.source: How brightly a blow's ground fills. Its edge stays whole.

menu.spire.motion.note.source: Nothing on the HUD pulses, flies or rises. Your system's own setting does the same.

menu.spire.palette.note.source: The color of a blow's edge, of safe ground and of a hazard.

menu.sync.note.source: Play offline by the same rules as online. This sets the settings that are fixed online to match. Everything else stays your choice.

menu.sync.same.source: Your offline game already plays by the online rules.

menu.sync.undoTip.source: {n, plural, one {Puts back the # setting the last sync changed} other {Puts back the # settings the last sync changed}}

menu.test.blurb.source: A ready-made character in the normal world, with one of every weapon, armor in every material, all four shields and spare clothes in the pack. Equip things from the inventory to see them on the paperdoll and in your hands, and on the Morrowind body if you have its data. Scroll to switch views. Nothing here touches your real saves.

menu.test.outdoorsNote.source: Pick a season and a weather, and drop into a random town. A test door: it stores nothing, and it names the town in the console.

menu.touch.analogNote.source: Push farther to run. Off: any push is a full step.

menu.touch.fullscreenNote.source: Fullscreen on the first touch. On iPhone, add the game to the home screen.

menu.touch.gyroSensitivityNote.source: Degrees of camera per degree of phone.

menu.touch.hapticsNote.source: A short buzz on presses, swings and locks.

menu.touch.lookNote.source: How far a drag turns the camera.

menu.touch.slotNote.source: The bottom-right buttons, from the corner in.

menu.transfer.app.source: This app keeps your saves as files in {path}. Export them as one zip to carry to the website, or import a zip the website exported.

menu.transfer.imported.source: Imported {n, plural, one {# save} other {# saves}}{skipped, plural, =0 {} other {, # already here}}{failed, plural, =0 {} other {, # could not be written}}.

menu.transfer.noneIn.source: No saves in that selection. Pick the zip an Export made, or a Saves folder holding SAVE0, SAVE1, ...

menu.transfer.title.source: Between the website and the app

menu.transfer.web.source: The website keeps your saves in this browser. Export them as one zip to carry to the desktop app or another browser, or import a zip the app or another browser exported.

mods.ambientText.Enabled.description.source: Now and then, a short line in the corner about where you are: what a crypt smells like, what a village sounds like at night, how the desert light looks. It depends on the place, the time and the weather, and stays quiet indoors.

mods.ambientText.interval.description.source: Real-time seconds between checks for a line

mods.ambientText.postTextInterval.descri.source: Real-time seconds to wait after a line is shown

mods.ambientText.textChance.description.source: Chance, in percent, of a line at each check

mods.ambientText.textDisplayTime.descrip.source: Seconds a line stays on screen

mods.betterAmbience.BetterFootsteps.enab.source: Plays Better Ambience’s own footstep sounds

mods.betterAmbience.BetterRain.enableBet.source: Makes rain particles look a bit better
Makes snow particles look a bit better

mods.betterAmbience.CameraShake.fadeInTi.source: Seconds the shake takes to build.

mods.betterAmbience.CameraShake.fadeOutT.source: Seconds the shake takes to settle.

mods.betterAmbience.CameraShake.maxShake.source: The most one hit can shake the camera.

mods.betterAmbience.CameraShake.roughnes.source: How jarring the shake is: lower is smoother.

mods.betterAmbience.CameraShake.shakeAmo.source: Shake added to every hit, before the hit’s own share.
Shake per hit, scaled by the damage as a share of your full health.

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonFog.enableFog.source: Gives each dungeon its own random fog

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonFog.maxFogDis.source: How far past its start the fog can reach, at most

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonFog.maxFogSta.source: Furthest from you the fog can start

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonFog.minFogDis.source: How far past its start the fog reaches, at least

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonFog.minFogSta.source: Nearest to you the fog can start

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonLighting.enab.source: Lights each dungeon in the color of its fog

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonLighting.fogA.source: How much the random dungeon color affects dungeon lighting

mods.betterAmbience.DungeonReverb.level..source: How much a dungeon echoes: Low is a cave, Medium a stone room, High a quarry.

mods.betterAmbience.Enabled.description.source: The camera shakes when you’re hurt, each dungeon gets its own fog, light and echo, and you can hear rain indoors.

mods.comeSailAway.Audio.SoundVolume.desc.source: Volume of the boat’s sounds: the hull, the oars and the sea.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.CargoThreshold.d.source: The weight a boat carries before it slows.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.CartCarriedWeigh.source: Count what your cart carries as cargo.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.CartItem.descrip.source: Count the cart itself as cargo.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.HorseItem.descri.source: Count the horse itself as cargo.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.PlayerCarriedWei.source: Count what you carry as cargo.

mods.comeSailAway.Cargo.PlayerWeight.des.source: Count your own weight as cargo.

mods.comeSailAway.Compatibility.Animated.source: Has no effect here: Animated Water isn’t included, so the mod’s own waves are always drawn.

mods.comeSailAway.Compatibility.Persiste.source: Keeps a boat you placed indoors or underground when you leave it. Off, the boat is gone once you’re back outside.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.DecreaseTimeS.source: Slow time back down at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.Disembark.des.source: Leave the helm (the Transport key does too).

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.IncreaseTimeS.source: Speed time up at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.PortLocationS.source: How far from you a port can be found

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.ResetTimeScal.source: Return time to normal speed at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.ToggleLight.d.source: Light or douse the boat’s lanterns at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.ToggleSail.de.source: Raise or stow the sails at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.TrimLeft.desc.source: Hold to trim the sails to the left (with Sailing Assist’s auto trimming off).

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.TrimModifier..source: Hold with a trim key to trim the square sails instead; hold with Toggle Sail to raise or stow the square sails alone.

mods.comeSailAway.Controls.TrimRight.des.source: Hold to trim the sails to the right (with Sailing Assist’s auto trimming off).

mods.comeSailAway.Debug.ShowValues.descr.source: Shows the boat’s speed, the speed it’s heading for and the wind’s strength on screen.

mods.comeSailAway.Enabled.description.source: Own and sail a boat. Buy parts or a deed at a shipyard, put it in the water (a deed works only near a port) and take the helm to row, or raise the sails and trim them to the wind. Pack it up to take with you. It holds what you and your cart carry and shows on the travel map.

mods.comeSailAway.Handling.OarMoveAccele.source: How quickly you reach top speed under oars.

mods.comeSailAway.Handling.OarTurnAccele.source: How quickly the oars turn the boat.

mods.comeSailAway.Handling.SailMoveAccel.source: How quickly you reach top speed under sail.

mods.comeSailAway.Handling.SailTurnAccel.source: How quickly the sails turn the boat.

mods.comeSailAway.Map.BackdropOpacity.de.source: How dark the screen behind the position reading is, in percent.

mods.comeSailAway.Map.ClickRangeThreshol.source: How near the pointer must come to a marker on the position reading, in map pixels, to name it or pick it.

mods.comeSailAway.Map.MarkerOutlineThick.source: Thickness of the marker outline in pixels

mods.comeSailAway.Map.MarkerThickness.de.source: Additional pixels around the map marker

mods.comeSailAway.Map.PositionLineThickn.source: Additional pixels on each side of the position line

mods.comeSailAway.Map.RestrictPositionRe.source: Position can only be viewed around midday and midnight
Position can only be viewed in Sunny or Cloudy weather

mods.comeSailAway.SailingAssist.AutoStow.source: Stow the square sails for you when you head into the wind.

mods.comeSailAway.SailingAssist.AutoTrim.source: Trim the sails to the wind for you.

mods.comeSailAway.Waves.Distance.descrip.source: How many map squares around you have waves, in each direction.

mods.comeSailAway.Waves.Enable.descripti.source: Draw the waves breaking along the coasts around you, and let the sea carry a boat on its current.

mods.comeSailAway.Waves.Fade.description.source: Where along their reach the waves start to fade.

mods.comeSailAway.Waves.Length.descripti.source: How far out the waves reach before they end.

mods.comeSailAway.Waves.Speed.descriptio.source: How fast the waves move: under 100 is half speed, 100 to 199 is normal, and 200 is fastest.

mods.comeSailAway.WindDirectionWidget.En.source: Show the wind’s direction on screen at the helm.

mods.comeSailAway.WindDirectionWidget.Po.source: Where the widget sits on the screen, across and down.

mods.comeSailAway.WindDirectionWidget.Sc.source: Whether the widget grows with the screen.

mods.comeSailAway.unread.description.source: Has no effect: the mod never uses this setting.

mods.daggerfallEnemyExpansion.DisableTro.source: Prevent trolls from respawning after death (use for No Magic runs)

mods.daggerfallEnemyExpansion.Enabled.de.source: Fifty new enemies - goblins, trolls, minotaurs, golems, mounted knights, necromancers, witches and more - in new encounter tables for every dungeon and climate.

mods.diverseWeapons.Enabled.description.source: A different first-person look for every weapon in every metal, plain and enchanted, instead of one per weapon type. A longsword no longer looks like a broadsword. A newer version added under Your own textures replaces the built-in one.

mods.diverseWeapons.WeaponWidgetPreset.d.source: Uses Diverse Weapons’ own Weapon Widget settings while on: larger idle poses, inertia, recoil and its own bob. Your Weapon Widget settings come back when you turn this off.

mods.dynamicSkies.ActivatePixelSnow.desc.source: Turn the pixel snow replacement on or off

mods.dynamicSkies.Enabled.description.source: A new sky for the enhanced outdoors, with cloud layers for each weather, twinkling stars, both moons, fog colors, longer sunrises and sunsets, and lightning in storms. Off uses the game’s own sky.

mods.dynamicSkies.MaxParticles.descripti.source: Has no effect: the mod never uses this setting.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Animation.FineBill.source: Added to BillboardScale, for a finer adjustment.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Animation.FineGlob.source: Has no effect: the mod never uses this setting.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Animation.GlobalOf.source: Has no effect: the mod never uses this setting.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Animation.SyncFoot.source: Footstep sounds match the sprite’s steps.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Animation.WalkCycl.source: Multiplier on how fast the walk cycle plays.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.AutoTogglePerspect.source: Which view to take on foot, with nothing readied.
Which view to take on foot with a weapon readied.
Which view to take on foot with a bow readied.
Which view to take on foot with a spell readied.
Which view to take in the saddle.
Which view to take in the saddle with something readied.
Which view to take on stepping back outside.
Which view to take on stepping indoors.
Key that turns the automatic view changes below on or off.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.AutoSwitch..source: Moves the camera to your other shoulder when there isn’t room

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.Dampen.desc.source: How much the camera lags behind a sudden move.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.MinimumDist.source: How close the camera may come to you, as a share of its distance.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.RidingOffse.source: Raises and pulls back the camera while you ride.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.Speed.descr.source: How fast the camera catches up to where it should be.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.StartInThir.source: Start in third person when you start or load a game

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.SwitchReset.source: Seconds before the camera switches back. 0 keeps it switched

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.SwitchShoul.source: Moves the camera to your other shoulder.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Camera.TogglePersp.source: Has no effect here: scroll the mouse wheel to change view.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.CameraOverrideBoat.source: Use the camera position below while sailing.
What the camera looks at while sailing.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.CameraOverrideMoun.source: Use the camera position below while riding.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.CameraOverrideWeap.source: Use the camera position below while a weapon or spell is readied.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.CameraScrolling.Sc.source: How far the camera moves with each scroll
Scroll to move the camera closer or further away
Has no effect here: the mouse wheel always moves the camera.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Compatibility.Dont.source: Keeps the first-person horse on screen in third person
Keeps the first-person weapon on screen in third person
Attacks start from the camera instead of your character’s body

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Debug.ShowMessages.source: Shows a message when the view or shoulder changes.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Enabled.descriptio.source: Third person without Morrowind data. Scroll out and the camera moves behind your shoulder, and you see yourself as the mod’s character sprite, on foot and on horseback. Off keeps you in first person unless you use the Morrowind body.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.FrontalPlaneOffset.source: Moves the camera sideways and up or down

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.AttackStr.source: Extra attack animations. Here PingPong looks the same as None, and Mixed the same as Mirror.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.FirstPers.source: Whether your character sprite shows in first person

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.MirrorTim.source: Seconds before a mirrored sprite turns back. 0 turns this off.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.PingPongO.source: Has no effect here: attacks never play backwards in this game.

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.ReadyStan.source: Whether the sprite will change states when readying a weapon or spell

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.ShowCart..source: A 3D cart follows you when you travel with your cart

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.TorchOffs.source: Whether the torch follows the orientation of the sprite

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.Graphics.TurnToVie.source: When the sprite turns to face where you look

mods.eyeOfTheBeholder.LongitudinalDistan.source: How far behind you the camera sits

mods.foraging.Enabled.description.source: Gather in the wilderness: chop wood with a Wood-Axe, mine gems and metals with a Pick-Axe, cut plants with a Sickle, rob graves with a Spade, fish with a Fishing-Net and forage for food with a Basket. You gather by day, away from towns and enemies, and your attributes, the climate and the season decide what you find.

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.BobWhileIdle.de.source: Whether the light will slightly bob while stationary

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.Length.descript.source: Amount of bobs in a single stride

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.Offset.descript.source: Advances the bob timing. For use with weapon bob.

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.SizeX.descripti.source: Extent of horizontal movement when bobbing

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.SizeY.descripti.source: Extent of vertical movement when bobbing

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.SpeedMove.descr.source: Speed of transition between stationary and moving

mods.handheldTorches.Bob.SpeedState.desc.source: Speed of transition between movement states

mods.handheldTorches.Compatibility.Textu.source: Divides a custom texture’s size. Raise it if a texture pack draws the hand too large.

mods.handheldTorches.Enabled.description.source: A lit torch, candle or lantern needs a free hand. You get keys to light, drop or throw one (a thrown torch can set an enemy on fire). You see the light in your hand in first person, and a dropped torch keeps burning, lights the room and can be picked up again.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.LanternsAt.source: If enabled, lanterns hang at your waist instead of being held, so they never need a free hand and are never put away. Torches and candles are still held.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.ManualDrop.source: Button used to manually drop a light source

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.OnPick.des.source: Behavior when picking up a light source

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.OnStow.des.source: Behavior when forced to stow a light source

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.RelaxedLan.source: If enabled, will not stow lanterns when both hands are occupied

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.RelaxedTwo.source: Two-handed weapons will only occupy your off-hand when attacking

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.RememberLa.source: Igniting with the key re-lights the light you last doused, if you still carry one.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.StowWhenCl.source: Climbing puts the light away to free your hand.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.StowWhenSp.source: Casting or readying a spell puts the light away to free your hand.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.StowWhenSw.source: Swimming puts the light away to free your hand.

mods.handheldTorches.Handling.ToggleLigh.source: Button used to quickly ignite or douse your light source

mods.handheldTorches.Inertia.ForwardDept.source: Multiplier for the change in scale when moving forward or backward

mods.handheldTorches.Inertia.ForwardSpee.source: The speed that the sprite will scale towards the target depth

mods.handheldTorches.Inertia.Scale.descr.source: The maximum distance that the sprite will be offset

mods.handheldTorches.Inertia.Speed.descr.source: The speed that the sprite will move at towards the target offset

mods.handheldTorches.Modules.Bob.descrip.source: Bob: the sprite sways as you walk, in step with Weapon Widget’s bob.

mods.handheldTorches.Modules.Inertia.des.source: Inertia: the light trails behind as you look around and move.

mods.handheldTorches.Modules.Sprite.desc.source: Sprite: a first-person hand holding the lit torch or lantern.

mods.handheldTorches.Modules.Step.descri.source: Step: the sprite’s position is rounded so it moves in steps.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.Ambide.source: Mirror the first-person graphic depending on the free hand. Recommended when using Shield Widget.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.AudioV.source: Volume of the burning loop and the torch sounds.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.LockAs.source: The sprite scales by the screen’s width alone, keeping its proportions.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.Offset.source: Where your hand rests on screen, across and up.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.Player.source: Plays a burning sound while you hold a torch

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.Speed..source: How fast the sprite slides on and off the screen.

mods.handheldTorches.Presentation.Tint.d.source: Matches the weapon sprite's tint when using First-Person-Lighting.

mods.handheldTorches.Step.Condition.desc.source: Whether the snapping only affects Sheathing or also other options like Bob, Inertia and Recoil

mods.handheldTorches.Step.Length.descrip.source: Size of each step. Higher moves in bigger jumps.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Accuracy.d.source: The to-hit modifier of the thrown torch.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Bounciness.source: How much speed a thrown torch keeps when it bounces.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Chance.des.source: % chance the fire takes on a struck foe.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Combustion.source: A thrown torch that strikes a foe can set it alight.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Duration.d.source: Rounds the fire burns on a struck foe.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Emission.d.source: A burning foe gives off light.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.EmissionSh.source: Has no effect here: a burning foe’s light casts no shadows in this game.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.GravityStr.source: Multiplies how fast a thrown torch falls.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.Magnitude..source: Fire damage per round, lowest and highest.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.ShowTrajec.source: Has no effect here: the throw’s arc isn’t drawn in this game.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.ThrowAngle.source: How many degrees above your aim the torch is thrown.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.ThrowDispe.source: Degrees of random spread on the throw.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.ThrowScale.source: How fast the wind-up charges while the key is held.

mods.handheldTorches.Throwing.ThrowTorch.source: Hold to wind up a throw, release to throw a torch.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Enabled.descripti.source: Your horse and cart stay in the world: they wait where you get off, follow you or stay on command, and you hitch or mount them by walking up to them. Online, other players see them where you left them.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Following.AvoidCo.source: A following horse, or horse and wagon, keeps away from enemies in a fight.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Following.FollowF.source: A following horse or wagon comes with you when you fast travel. Off, it waits where it was.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Following.HorseFo.source: How closely a following horse, or horse and wagon, stays behind you.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Hotkeys.QuickMoun.source: Mounts your last-used horse or wagon if it’s in reach, or dismounts if you’re riding. Click it and press a key to change it; ✕ clears it.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Hotkeys.SummonTra.source: Brings your horse and wagon to you when you’re outdoors. Click it and press a key to change it; ✕ clears it.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Persistence.Physi.source: Your horse and wagon stay where you leave them. Off, they are always with you, as in the classic game.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Presentation.Show.source: Shows the wagon trailing behind you when you ride with your cart. Off hides only that wagon.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.WagonAccess.Inter.source: How close to a building or dungeon entrance your wagon must be for you to use it from inside.

mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.Enabled.descripti.source: A real sea: the seafloor drops away from every coast to as deep as 250 meters. Swim in open water with a breath meter among fish, weed, coral, shipwrecks, sunken loot and whatever lives in the deep.

mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.Decoratio.source: How far from you the seafloor is decorated, in map squares. At 3 nothing pops in

mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.EnableSwi.source: Press Run while swimming for a burst of speed

mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.MaxDecora.source: Maximum decorations per map square. Lower runs faster

mods.immersiveFootsteps.ArmorSwaySetting.source: Your armor makes a sound as you move
How often armor sounds play. Lower is more often

mods.immersiveFootsteps.Enabled.descript.source: Footsteps that match the ground you walk on, and armour that rattles as you move.

mods.immersiveFootsteps.ErrorLoggingAndC.source: Warns you when another mod clashes with this one
Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.
Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.

mods.immersiveFootsteps.FootstepSettings.source: How often footsteps sound. Lower is more often

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.Enabled.de.source: Level up like Oblivion Remastered: every skill you raise fills a 100-point bar, and each level gives you virtues to spend on the attributes you choose. New characters are asked which system they want.

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.allowLuckI.source: Allow Luck to be increased by more than one point

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.attributeP.source: Amount of points for increasing attributes

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.luckIncrea.source: Cost to upgrade Luck by one point

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.majorSkill.source: Points given by a Major Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.maxUpdatab.source: The number of attributes to be increased in one level up

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.minorSkill.source: Points given by a Minor Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.miscSkills.source: Points given by a Misc Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.primarySki.source: Points given by a Primary Skill level up (100 points required to level up). Morrowind has no Primary skills, so this starts equal to Major skills.

mods.oceanHoles.Enabled.description.source: Blue holes in the deep sea lead down to flooded dungeons with better loot. About 1 open-sea square in 48 has one: a black hole in the seafloor under a cloud of dark mist. Needs Iliac Puddle No More.

mods.oceanHoles.General.DungeonVisualDar.source: How dark the fog and light are in flooded dungeons

mods.oceanHoles.General.MiasmaHeight.des.source: Height of the mist over a hole

mods.oceanHoles.General.MiasmaParticleCo.source: Amount of mist over a hole

mods.oceanHoles.General.PitSpawnRate.des.source: How many blue holes there are: none at 0, 1 square in 48 at the middle, 1 in 24 at most

mods.pcaao.Enabled.description.source: Armour reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, your skills decide whether you hit, shields block according to their material, and critical hits multiply damage. Off uses Daggerfall Unity’s combat.

mods.pcaao.armorHitFormulaRedone.descrip.source: Armor reduces the damage you take instead of making you harder to hit.

mods.pcaao.conditionBasedEffectiveness.d.source: Worn weapons and armor work less well. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.pcaao.criticalStrikesIncreaseDamage.source: Critical strikes raise your damage as well as your chance to hit. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.pcaao.equipmentDamageEnhanced.descr.source: Your equipment wears out much faster, depending on its material, what hit it and more.

mods.pcaao.fadingEnchantedItems.descript.source: Enchanted weapons and armor are destroyed when they break in combat. Needs Equipment Damage Enhanced.

mods.pcaao.fixedStrengthDamageModifier.d.source: Strength adds 1 damage per 10 points, as in the classic game, instead of 2.

mods.pcaao.softMaterialRequirements.desc.source: Weapons below the material an enemy needs can still hurt it, at a large damage penalty. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.roadsHazelnut.Enabled.description.source: Hazelnut’s roads, tracks, rivers and streams across the whole Iliac Bay, painted onto the land. Off, the game builds its own roads between the towns on your map.

mods.roadsHazelnut.RiversAndStreams.desc.source: Draws rivers and streams on the land.

mods.roadsHazelnut.SmoothRoads.descripti.source: Lightly smooths road surfaces. Turn it off for slightly better performance.

mods.roleplayRealism.Enabled.description.source: Realism changes: bows by draw weight, no climbing with a weapon out, fairer swing speed and hit chance, bank loans by level, ships only from ports, a heavy-load penalty, lights out when you leave a dungeon, purification that cures poison, reworked class enemies, harsher guild expulsions, and beds you can click to sleep in.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Gall.source: Enables galloping (sprinting) while riding horses in towns.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Real.source: Makes the horse and cart movement backwards and sideways more realistic and limited.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Tram.source: Enables the crime of trampling innocent townsfolk when galloping in a town. Be careful!

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.enha.source: Enable enhanced horse riding module, improving presentation and allowing galloping.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.foll.source: How much the ride smooths out slopes, from 0 (none) to 32 (most).

mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.int.source: Enables intensive training option for a session per day for five days, for extra cost.

mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.var.source: Makes price of training based on skill level as well as player level.

mods.roleplayRealism.advancedArchery.des.source: Alters to-hit and damage done by arrows depending on the length of draw.

mods.roleplayRealism.autoExtinguishLight.source: Automatically extinguish any light sources when you exit a dungeon

mods.roleplayRealism.bandaging.descripti.source: Allows bandages to be used for healing based on medical skill.

mods.roleplayRealism.bedSleeping.descrip.source: Allows sleep to be initiated by clicking on a bed.

mods.roleplayRealism.classicStrengthDama.source: Shows the strength damage bonus at half, as the classic game did.

mods.roleplayRealism.climbingRestriction.source: Prevents climbing with a weapon drawn.

mods.roleplayRealism.encumbranceEffects..source: Provides speed and fatigue penalties when carrying too much weight.

mods.roleplayRealism.enemyAppearance.des.source: Remixes human enemy appearance based on class

mods.roleplayRealism.equipDamage.descrip.source: Increases equipment damage proportional to max condition.

mods.roleplayRealism.loanAmountPerLevel..source: Sets the maximum amount per level that can be borrowed from banks

mods.roleplayRealism.purificationPotion..source: Changes purification potion to cure poison rather than grant invisibility

mods.roleplayRealism.shipPorts.descripti.source: Player can only board their ship when in a port town.

mods.roleplayRealism.underworldExpulsion.source: Enables underworld guilds to expel members for poor performance... with prejudice.

mods.roleplayRealism.variantNpcs.descrip.source: Enable variant NPC sprites in shops & taverns

mods.roleplayRealism.variantResidents.de.source: Fills 80% of houses with the townsfolk you see walking around, instead of random adventurers

mods.roleplayRealism.weaponMaterials.des.source: Moderates the to-hit bonuses of weapon materials so skill remains key factor

mods.roleplayRealism.weaponSpeed.descrip.source: Lowers weapon damage per second for characters with high Speed.

mods.roleplayRealismItems.Enabled.descri.source: Adds 2 new weapons and light and medium armor sets in every metal, and changes what items weigh and cost.

mods.roleplayRealismItems.alchemistPotio.source: Adds random potions for sale at alchemist stores, for a premium price

mods.roleplayRealismItems.bandaging.desc.source: Allows bandages to stack, and to be used for healing based on medical skill

mods.roleplayRealismItems.conditionBased.source: Item prices are based on condition and loot you find can be quite worn out

mods.roleplayRealismItems.lootRebalance..source: Rebalances loot on mobs and in piles

mods.roleplayRealismItems.newArmor.descr.source: Adds new chest, arm, leg and foot armor pieces to the game

mods.roleplayRealismItems.newWeapons.des.source: Adds two new weapons to the game, Archers Axe and Light Flail

mods.roleplayRealismItems.realisticEnemy.source: Enemy equipment is realistic for their class and can be variable condition

mods.roleplayRealismItems.skillBasedStar.source: Player starting equipment is based on skills
Player starting spells are based on skills

mods.roleplayRealismItems.storeQualityIt.source: Items in shops can be in a used condition dependent on the quality of the store

mods.roleplayRealismItems.weaponBalance..source: Balances weapon attack speed and damage ranges against weight to give more valid choices

mods.seasonsIliacBay.Enabled.description.source: Trees, rocks and plants change with autumn, spring and winter. Add your own copy of the mod under Your own textures, or the classic look is used.

mods.shieldWidget.Animation.Direction.de.source: Set which animations will play during actions

mods.shieldWidget.Animation.Speed.descri.source: Determines how fast the animation plays

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.BobWhileIdle.descr.source: Whether the shield will slightly bob while stationary

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.Length.description.source: Amount of bobs in a single stride

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.Offset.description.source: Advances the bob timing. For use with weapon bob.

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.SizeX.description.source: Extent of horizontal movement when bobbing

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.SizeY.description.source: Extent of vertical movement when bobbing

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.SpeedMove.descript.source: Speed of transition between stationary and moving

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.SpeedState.descrip.source: Speed of transition between movement states

mods.shieldWidget.Compatibility.TextureS.source: Divides the sprite’s pixel size. Raise it if a replacement texture pack draws the shield too large.

mods.shieldWidget.Enabled.description.source: See your shield in first person, which the original game never shows. It is drawn in its own metal, gets battered as it wears, and moves out of the way when you sheathe, swing or cast.

mods.shieldWidget.Inertia.ForwardDepth.d.source: Multiplier for the change in scale when moving forward or backward

mods.shieldWidget.Inertia.ForwardSpeed.d.source: The speed that the sprite will scale towards the target depth

mods.shieldWidget.Inertia.Scale.descript.source: The maximum distance that the sprite will be offset

mods.shieldWidget.Inertia.Speed.descript.source: The speed that the sprite will move at towards the target offset

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Animation.desc.source: Animation: the shield is raised and lowered frame by frame instead of sliding (art by WilhelmBlack).

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Bob.descriptio.source: Bob: the shield sways as you walk.

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Inertia.descri.source: Inertia: the shield trails behind as you look around and move.

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Recoil.descrip.source: Recoil: a blow that lands on the shield rocks it and makes it ring. Needs Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul.

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Step.descripti.source: Step: the shield’s position is rounded so it moves in steps.

mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Condition.descr.source: Event required for the shield to recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Offset.descript.source: Whether the shield should be moved to the center when recoiling

mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Scale.descripti.source: The amount the shield will recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Speed.descripti.source: The speed that the shield recovers from recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.ConditionThresh.source: Condition, in percent, below which the shield looks badly damaged.
Condition, in percent, below which the shield first looks damaged.

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.LockAspectRatio.source: Enable to prevent the sprite from stretching or squishing depending on the screen's aspect ratio

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.OffsetHorizonta.source: Offsets the sprite relative to the left edge of the screen

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.OffsetVertical..source: Offsets the sprite relative to the bottom edge of the screen

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.Speed.descripti.source: Speed of stance transition when attacking

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenAttacking.d.source: The shield's behavior when attacking with a weapon

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenCasting.des.source: The shield's behavior when readying or while casting a spell

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenSheathed.de.source: The shield's behavior when sheathing your weapon

mods.shieldWidget.Step.Condition.descrip.source: Whether the snapping only affects Sheathing or also other options like Bob, Inertia and Recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Step.Length.descriptio.source: Size of each step. Higher moves in bigger jumps.

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.Fatigu.source: Level of fatigue that will automatically pause the journey when travelling cautiously, absolute value

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.Health.source: Level of health that will automatically pause the journey when travelling cautiously, as a percentage

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.MaxCha.source: Maximum chance to avoid an encounter when travelling cautiously, as a percentage

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.Player.source: Enables the travel option "Cautiously" to initiate time accelerated travel, instead of vanilla fast travel

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.SpeedP.source: Speed penalty for travelling cautiously, as a percentage

mods.travelOptions.Enabled.description.source: Choose between the original game’s fast travel and a journey you make yourself, sped up to 60 times, with a panel to steer it. Encounters and places along the way stop you, and you can follow the roads. Off brings back the classic travel map with fast travel only.

mods.travelOptions.FastTravelCostScaling.source: Scales the cost of inns when using standard fast travel, suggest x4-x6 for Climate & Calories.
Scales the cost of ships when using standard fast travel, suggest x2-x3 for Climate & Calories.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowA.source: Allows footstep and hoof sounds during time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowR.source: Has no effect here: Real Grass isn’t included.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowT.source: Allows travel map to target any coordinates using time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowW.source: Allows weather effects during time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AvoidO.source: Steers time accelerated travel around buildings, walls and rocks, and pauses the journey before walking into something it can’t get round.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.FirstP.source: Makes time accelerated journeys in first person, on the ground. Off, the enhanced interface makes them in the Overworld view. Takes effect at once.

With First Person Travel on, journeys follow the roads and tracks as Overworld journeys do, and a place with no way there by land can’t be picked. Off, you head straight for your destination. Takes effect at once.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.Locati.source: Auto pause when encountering a game location during real time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.LocationColours.descr.source: The colour shown on the travel map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Enab.source: Enhances the travel map with larger location dots for cities & towns, and shows roads & tracks with toggle buttons
Adds a streams toggle button separate from rivers button
Enhances the travel map with rivers and streams with a toggle button

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Foll.source: Custom key bind for following paths used if CustomBind set above
Sets the key to initiate time accelerated travelling following paths if roads integration enabled

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Mark.source: The colour used to highlight locations using middle mouse button on travel map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Vari.source: All locations, except for cities & towns, are rendered as smaller dots

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Back.source: The opaque background color to use for the mini-map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Circ.source: Draw the mini-map in a circle around the player

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Filt.source: Pixel filtering to use when rendering the mini-map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Opaq.source: Render the mini-map with an opaque background color

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Pers.source: Set this to have the junction mini-map always displayed when following paths

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Play.source: The colour of the player position and direction indicator

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Scre.source: The X coordinate the mini-map is rendered on the screen
The Y coordinate the mini-map is rendered on the screen
The width and height the mini-map is rendered on the screen

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Togg.source: Set this to have the junction mini-map toggled when follow key pressed and not on a path

mods.travelOptions.ShipTravel.OnlyFromPo.source: Restricts ship travel to be possible only from places with ports

mods.travelOptions.ShipTravel.OnlyToPort.source: Restricts ship travel to be possible only if destination has a port, if from ports setting is enabled

mods.travelOptions.StopAtInnsTravel.Play.source: Enables the stop for night travel option "Inns" to initiate time accelerated travel, instead of fast travel

mods.travelOptions.Teleportation.EnableP.source: Enable paid Mages teleportation service for all guild members, before rank 8

mods.unleveledLoot.Enabled.description.source: Loot and shop stock no longer scale with your level. What materials drop depends on your luck, the shop’s quality and the type of dungeon, and the gold you find follows your luck. Off uses Daggerfall Unity’s rolls.

mods.unleveledLoot.MaterialSwitching.des.source: Whenever this material would drop, change it to the selected material.

mods.warmAshesShips.Enabled.description.source: When you travel by ship, 1 trip in 4 is attacked by pirates. You fight them on deck beside your crew, on a borrowed ship if you don’t own one, then land where you were going.

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.BobWhileIdle.descr.source: Whether the weapon will slightly bob while stationary

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.Length.description.source: Amount of bobs in a single stride

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.Offset.description.source: Advances the bob timing. For use with weapon bob.

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.SizeX.description.source: Extent of horizontal movement when bobbing

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.SizeY.description.source: Extent of vertical movement when bobbing

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.SpeedMove.descript.source: Speed of transition between stationary and moving

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.SpeedState.descrip.source: Speed of transition between movement states

mods.weaponWidget.Enabled.description.source: Livelier first-person weapons: swings that wind up and recover, the weapon in the hand you swing with, a sheathe animation, a bob as you walk, sway as you look and a kick when you hit or parry. The Morrowind arms move the same way.

mods.weaponWidget.Inertia.ForwardDepth.d.source: Multiplier for the change in scale when moving forward or backward

mods.weaponWidget.Inertia.ForwardSpeed.d.source: The speed that the sprite will scale towards the target depth

mods.weaponWidget.Inertia.Scale.descript.source: The maximum distance that the sprite will be offset

mods.weaponWidget.Inertia.Speed.descript.source: The speed that the sprite will move at towards the target offset

mods.weaponWidget.Miscellaneous.MirrorTw.source: Draws a two-handed axe mirrored in the right hand.
Draws a two-handed staff, hammer or flail mirrored in the right hand.
Draws a two-handed sword mirrored in the right hand.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Ambidexterity..source: Ambidexterity: the weapon shows in the hand you swing with (Switch Hand, H), mirrored for the left.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Bob.descriptio.source: Bob: the sprite sways as you walk.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.DoubleScaleTex.source: DoubleScaleTextures: draws the idle pose at double size from the mod’s own textures. Add the mod’s .dfmod under Your own textures.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Inertia.descri.source: Inertia: the weapon trails behind as you look around and move. Needs double-scaled weapon textures.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Offset.descrip.source: Offset: sheathing slides the sprite off the screen and drawing slides it back; a swing returns from below.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Recoil.descrip.source: Recoil: the swing bounces back on a hit, parry or miss, as set below.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Step.descripti.source: Step: the sprite’s position is rounded so it moves in steps.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Swings.descrip.source: Swings: each strike winds up from the idle pose, plays at its own speed and recovers, in reverse after a hit.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.TrueTextureSiz.source: TrueTextureSize: a custom texture is drawn at its own pixel size, divided by the scale factor below.

mods.weaponWidget.Offset.Speed.descripti.source: Speed of the slide on and off the screen.

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.Chance.descript.source: Chance, in percent, of a recoil when the condition is met

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.DetectEnvironme.source: A swing into a wall or a door within reach recoils too.

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.MissEffectPlace.source: Where the clang or thud is drawn.

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.PlayEntityMissE.source: A clang or a thud at a foe that parried or was missed.

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.PlayEnvironment.source: A thud where the swing met the wall.

mods.weaponWidget.Step.Condition.descrip.source: Whether the snapping only affects Sheathing or also other options like Bob, Inertia and Recoil

mods.weaponWidget.Step.Length.descriptio.source: Size of each step. Higher moves in bigger jumps.

mods.weaponWidget.Swings.NoDaggerMirrore.source: Prevents Daggers from using the opposite hand animations

mods.weaponWidget.Swings.Recovery.descri.source: What shows while the swing recovers.

mods.weaponWidget.Swings.VanillaAlignmen.source: Centres the down and up strikes of the vanilla weapons at the screen’s middle edge.

mods.weaponWidget.Swings.VanillaRecovery.source: Plays the StrikeUp animation in reverse during recovery for some vanilla weapons

mods.weaponWidget.Swings.Windup.descript.source: What shows while the swing winds up.

mods.weaponWidget.TrueTextureSize.Textur.source: With True Texture Size on, divides a custom texture’s size. Raise it if the weapon draws too large.

mods.worldEventsRaidingParties.Enabled.d.source: Knights, bandits or orcs raid towns across Tamriel for 2 hours. With the town guard, beat 15 to 25 raiders to free the town and raise your standing in the region. Online, everyone in town fights the same raid.

mods.worldOfDaggerfall.Enabled.descripti.source: More to find in the wilderness: bandit camps and forts, ruins, shrines, mountains and rock fields across the Iliac Bay, with bandits, bears and treasure, and a camp outside Privateer’s Hold.

mods.worldTooltips.Enabled.description.source: Shows the name of what you’re looking at under the crosshair: people, shops and their opening hours, doors and their locks, where an exit leads, levers, ladders, bookshelves and Daedra waiting to be summoned. Off, you still see what a chest or body holds.

mods.worldTooltips.HideDefaultInteractTo.source: Hides the label on things that may be meant to stay secret, such as the puzzles of the main quest.

monument.count.source: You have laid {n, plural, one {# flower} other {# flowers}} here

monument.steal.source: You leave the flowers where they lie.

monument.stewart.laid.source: You lay flowers for Patrick Stewart.

monument.stewart.read.source: He gave his voice to Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion.

monument.stewart.voice.source: The voice of Emperor Uriel Septim VII

monument.travelers.source: Travelers lay flowers at his stone.

music.box.none.source: The music box has no tunes yet. Foes sometimes drop sheet music. Use a sheet to add its tune.

music.sheet.known.source: Your music box can already play {tune}. You can sell this sheet.

music.sheet.learned.source: Your music box can now play {tune}.

naval.cloth.armsOff.source: Put my guild's arms on the sails

naval.cloth.armsOn.source: Your guild's arms on the sails

naval.cloth.shut.source: Buy the Guild Sailcloth on your guild's Shop page to use sail patterns and your guild's arms.

naval.deck.bad.source: Those fittings can't be placed on this ship.

naval.deck.cleared.source: All fittings removed. Click Save layout to keep this.

naval.deck.full.source: A deck holds at most {max} fittings.

naval.deck.hint.source: Pick a fitting, then click the deck to place it. Click a placed fitting to select and drag it.

naval.deck.offDeck.source: That spot isn't on the open deck.

naval.deck.set.source: Deck layout saved: {n, plural, one {# fitting} other {# fittings}}.

naval.deck.taken.source: {what} selected. Drag to move, Q/E to turn, Del to remove.

naval.deck.unknown.source: The deck isn't loaded yet. Place the ship in the world first.

naval.figurehead.done.source: Figurehead carved. Other players will see it.

naval.figurehead.noStem.source: This ship has no stem for a figurehead.

naval.figurehead.note.source: Free. It takes the ship's trim paint, or gilt. Other players see it.

naval.flag.guildNote.source: The ship flies your guild's arms in this shape and updates when they change.

naval.flag.noArms.source: Your guild has no arms, or you're not in a guild.

naval.flag.noMast.source: This ship has no masthead for a flag.

naval.flag.struck.source: Flag removed. The ship flies the default pennant.

naval.hold.noSea.source: Come Sail Away is not running.

naval.hold.noShip.source: You have no ship with a hold.

naval.ore.adamantium.source: Adamantium ingots, or an adamantium weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.daedric.source: Daedric ingots, or a daedric weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.dwarven.source: Dwarven ingots, or a dwarven weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.ebony.source: Ebony or Warforged Steel ingots, or an ebony weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.elven.source: Moonstone ingots, or an elven weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.mithril.source: Mithril ingots, or a mithril weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.orcish.source: Orichalcum ingots, or an orcish weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.silver.source: Silver ingots, or a silver weapon or plate melted down

naval.ore.steel.source: Steel ingots, or a steel weapon or plate melted down

naval.paint.bare.source: Paint removed. The ship is back to its original look.

net.conduct.spam.source: No spam, no scams, and no pretending to be staff.

poi.review.kindRollback.source: put revision {rev} back in the world

poi.review.more.source: More submissions are waiting. Decide on these to see the rest.

poi.review.needWord.source: Say why it goes back. The builder reads it.

poi.uv.noPicture.source: This material has no picture, so there are no pixels to set a density by.

poi.uv.packNoRoom.source: The islands do not fit in the square at that margin. Nothing was moved. Try a smaller margin.

poi.uv.unwrapHint.source: Lays the selection flat, keeping its angles. Marked seams are cut open.

poi.uv.unwrapped.source: Unwrapped {n, plural, one {# island} other {# islands}}.
